Gina

subject: An update on early voting numbers in key battleground states:
body:
We’re only sending this to our most engaged supporters [ ](https://ak.democrats.org/go/87341?t=1&akid=9996%2E22930333%2E_CVewr)
---
Derek, this is an email from the Democratic National Committee about our work to flip Congress in 13 days. If you need help checking your voter registration or making a plan to vote, please visit [iwillvote.com](https://ak.democrats.org/go/9784?t=2&akid=9996%2E22930333%2E_CVewr). If you'd prefer to [receive fewer emails](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/receive-less-email/?t=3&akid=9996%2E22930333%2E_CVewr) or [stop receiving our emails](https://ak.democrats.org/cms/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?t=4&akid=9996%2E22930333%2E_CVewr), you can click [here](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/receive-less-email/?t=5&akid=9996%2E22930333%2E_CVewr). Derek, **Early voting is officially underway in many states across the country.** As one of our top grassroots supporters, we want to keep you in the loop on the DNC’s strategy for the final 13 days before Election Day. Please take a minute to read this memo — we made this specifically for our most engaged supporters. _**2026 Early Voting Update for Derek Willis_**
* As of this morning, voters are casting their ballots in 37 states. **That means time is running out to turn out voters in key battlegrounds and help them make a plan to vote.**
* Currently, early voting in **Georgia is pacing _ahead_** of early voting numbers during the 2022 midterm elections, and polling favors Democrats maintaining their hold on this critical Senate seat.
* In **North Carolina, Democrats need to _flip_ the open Senate seat** to help take the majority this year and are currently **pacing ahead of their early ballots returned at this point in 2022.** Democrats have consistently led Republicans in polling this year, but turnout will be key.
* **Democrats are also working to flip a Senate seat in Iowa this year.** Currently, early ballots returned are **outpacing this point in 2022,** and polling predicts an incredibly tight race. Traditionally, most Iowans return their ballots on Election Day, so there’s still a chance to reach as many voters as possible across the state, help them make their voices heard, and flip this seat.
* **Michigan is currently pacing close to its early vote numbers from 2022, but there’s still time to change that if we act now.** This is a _must-win state_ for Democrats if we want to flip the Senate this year, and **polling currently shows that the race is neck and neck.**
* **Maine's Senate seat** is another must-flip seat for Democrats this year. Currently **leading ahead of early vote numbers from 2022,** this will also be an incredibly tight race.
* In **Ohio,** Democrats are also working to flip the Senate seat to win a majority, and the race is rated as another toss-up. Most Ohioans vote on Election Day, so it’s critical that we ensure every Ohio Democrat is ready to cast their ballot come November 3.

With just 13 days until Election Day, the DNC is strategically moving resources to the states and districts across the country that need the most support in these final weeks. We’re deploying organizers and volunteers to key districts to knock doors, we’re sending poll observers to polling locations to ensure the election is free, fair, and the results are trustworthy, and we’re making calls every day into states across the country to reach voters we might not otherwise. Derek, we hope you found this memo helpful. Keeping our top grassroots supporters fully informed and up-to-date on our strategic priorities is a top priority for our team. [**We hope you’ll consider chipping in today to fund our on-the-ground organizing efforts in the final days before Election Day and help lay the groundwork to win this year and beyond. The DNC is best positioned to distribute resources where and when they’re needed most, and every dollar we receive goes directly to the front lines to elect Democrats up and down the ballot nationwide.**](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-dnc-october-2026-gfr.AWsDfI&refcode=em_20261021_9996_fr&amount=7&t=6&akid=9996%2E22930333%2E_CVewr) _If you 've stored your info with ActBlue, we'll process your contribution instantly._ | | | **[Donate $7](https://ak.democrats.org/go/89866?c0=em-dnc-october-2026-gfr.GS9qR7&amount=7&refcode=em_20261021_9996_fr&t=7&akid=9996%2E22930333%2E_CVewr)**

[1] He claims to support term limits, but has already broken his pledge to serve no more than 12 years in the House. [2] He insists he's committed to protecting children, yet he's done nothing to demand accountability or unseal the most infamous case of child endangerment, the Epstein files. ---
Hi friend, it's Deb.

With Election Day right around the corner, I’ve been on the road, listening to as many New Mexicans as I can. My focus is making sure people have the opportunity to ask questions, share what’s on their minds, and hear directly from me about my vision for New Mexico’s future before they head to the polls.
The energy on the ground is incredible! Folks all over our state are ready to build a future where everyone can thrive. **[_If you’re ready to make this a reality, will you chip in $5 right now so I can reach the final undecided voters in these last 13 days and win?_](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17378?refcode=jtk1591-fr-nd&t=2&akid=13368%2E400544%2EOxzB6W)**
| | [Pitch in $5 >>](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17378?refcode=jtk1591-fr-nd&t=3&akid=13368%2E400544%2EOxzB6W)
---
Here’s a look at some of the stops I’ve made in _just_ the past week:
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17370?refcode=jtk1591-fr-nd&t=4&akid=13368%2E400544%2EOxzB6W)
I spoke to voters in the South Valley about how high the stakes are at this moment — from the affordability crisis and Trump’s reckless attacks on our state to our fight to protect our sacred land for future generations.

Each conversation reminds me what makes New Mexico so special — and why it’s so important to keep fighting for a better future.
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17370?refcode=jtk1591-fr-nd&t=5&akid=13368%2E400544%2EOxzB6W)
I joined a meeting of the organization Drinking Liberally in Albuquerque to answer questions about my plan to improve schools, increase access to healthcare, and build safer communities for our families. I made it clear that I’m ready to deliver real results and get things done for New Mexicans.
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17370?refcode=jtk1591-fr-nd&t=6&akid=13368%2E400544%2EOxzB6W)
I was joined by Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer in Rio Rancho, where we discussed the importance of Democratic governors who serve as firewalls against federal abuses of power. With Trump escalating his attacks on New Mexico, we need proven leaders who will protect our fundamental rights, our land, and our people.
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17370?refcode=jtk1591-fr-nd&t=7&akid=13368%2E400544%2EOxzB6W)
I was joined by Sen. Elizabeth Warren to discuss the crucial need to protect and expand universal childcare in New Mexico and how my plan to lower costs, build more homes, and cut the red tape to make home buying easier for first-time homeowners will support New Mexicans.

Every conversation has been a powerful reminder of why I’m running: to listen, bring people together, and deliver real results for families in every corner of our state. All across our beautiful state, New Mexicans want the same things: affordable, accessible healthcare, a strong education for their kids, safe communities, and the ability to pay the rent and buy groceries in the same month.
That’s what I’m fighting for. **_But right now, we’re running out of time to make sure we keep New Mexico blue._**
**With only 13 days until Election Day, every door, every conversation, and every vote matters more than ever before.[_Please, will you chip in $5 or more right now to help power my campaign for Governor and reach voters in every corner of New Mexico?_](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17370?refcode=jtk1591-fr-nd&t=8&akid=13368%2E400544%2EOxzB6W)**
| | [Pitch in $5 >>](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17378?refcode=jtk1591-fr-nd&t=9&akid=13368%2E400544%2EOxzB6W)
---
Together, we’re going to build a New Mexico for all New Mexicans.

Thank you, and be fierce,
Deb

Peter, Have you heard? Do you feel it? [Early](https://clicksp.votejustinearly.com/f/a/zEGAvwyfzIHN8bQh1v3SgA~~/AAPPABA~/mc23ckxzL-W5sU-v7HBT3DrvOJpWBv_Zhg3ajiogun2zOsU8Qg5WlNMc90Ezp9YxYm6-MjVnTtMN5TLf1OeKBo3kuN1pIVJkuNQAOv88AYARi-QE8KeOZ0DcnG3J2Qs2vfztCJJSkO_iUFL8FQN8WBR9eoB_d7CDD9NdK3rlh3BOhKW5s8kXXMz3AYf23p4Qw-U07uqAwxdEunxchCe_yHF8xiL8PSBqRFrmvDIKew5re5jP5NJdEGuTd68jjvZvZ9KCIQIPCoZU07iFKxXTsg~~) voting is underway, and our district is show up in a **big** way! In Bell County, near center of TX-31, 8,796 people voted on day one, a midterm record. In-person turnout was more than 50% above opening day in 2022, and over 14,000 people voted in person in the first two days. In Williamson County, about 13,500 had voted by 2 p.m. on opening day, nearly matching the roughly 15,000 who voted on the entire first day in 2022. This surge builds on a record-setting primary, when Democratic early turnout jumped 123% over 2022. Texas also has about 1.4 million more registered voters than it did four years ago. And earlier this year, Democrat Taylor Rehmet won the Senate District 9 runoff by 14 points in a district Trump carried by 17. We have a movement! Turnout alone does not tell us who people voted for, but analysts say Democrats are more enthusiastic this cycle. When a district that has been taken for granted wakes up, seats flip. Let's flip this seat! Here is how you can help:

| | Peter,

I just walked off the debate stage where one thing was clear: We need leaders who are going to put Minnesota first.

If you need help checking your voter registration or making a plan to vote, please visit [iwillvote.com](https://ak.democrats.org/go/9784?t=2&akid=10019%2E22930333%2E6H1oTv). subject: You’re one of a select few
body:
Hey, Peter – I wanted to reach out directly.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1728&source=&t=1&akid=4821%2E124072%2EZ9Ya5k) | | | |

Peter, not everyone will be getting this email.
I’m only reaching out to a select group of folks – people who haven’t donated to our campaign yet, but have stayed engaged with our updates and might be inclined to chip in for the first time today. **Your name was on that list.**
First, I want to say thank you for even opening this message. Your inbox is likely packed with emails like this right now, so I don’t take your time and attention for granted.
Here’s the deal: **The deadline to hit our fundraising goal to fund our FINAL TV ads before Election Day is at 11:59 p.m. tonight. To ensure we have the resources to reach every last voter between now and Nov. 3, I set an ambitious $500,000 goal for our team to reach before then.**
Frankly, we’re running out of time to make our case to North Carolinians – and a recent poll of likely voters shows that 7% are still undecided.
If they all end up siding with my MAGA opponent because we let far-right super PACs have the final word on the airwaves, **our lead in this race could shrink overnight.** With Senate control at stake here, that’s a risk we simply cannot afford to take.
Unlike my opponent, Michael Whatley, this campaign is not bankrolled by billionaires. More than 95% of our donations last quarter were $100 or less, so when I say this movement is powered by small-dollar support from people like you, I mean it, Peter.
**That’s why I’m personally asking for your help today.[_Will you please chip in your first $5 donation to help us reach this ambitious goal by the midnight deadline? The results of this battleground race will shape the future of our country, so your support couldn’t come at a more urgent time._](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1728&amount=5&t=8&akid=4821%2E124072%2EZ9Ya5k)**

Roy Cooper

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

name: Kylie Glatfelter
subject: Beau Bayh Can't Have It Both Ways on Girls' Sports
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY THE INDIANA REPUBLICAN STATE COMMITTEE
body:
No images? [Click here](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-e-fdtijuy-hhlljjcji-x/) **For Immediate Release:** October 21, 2026**Contact:** Kylie Glatfelter, Communications Director, [kglatfelter@indiana.gop](mailto:kglatfelter@indiana.gop)**Beau Bayh Is Proud to Have JD Ford on His Team. What Does That Say About His Judgment?****Indianapolis, Ind. **- Of all the endorsements Beau Bayh could have celebrated, he chose one from a senator who voted against protecting girls' sports, against extending those protections to women's college athletics, and against banning gender-transition procedures for minors.In June, Bayh posted on [social media](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fdtijuy-hhlljjcji-r/): "Honored to have earned the endorsement of my friend, State Senator JD Ford. I'm proud to have you on our team!" When the [Indiana Capital Chronicle](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fdtijuy-hhlljjcji-y/) asked Bayh if he supports Indiana's ban on boys in girls' sports, he waved the whole thing away as a "nonissue." Ford voted against the [2022 law](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fdtijuy-hhlljjcji-j/) protecting girls' sports, which took effect after Republicans overrode a veto. His reasoning? He said it "does not solve an issue." In 2025, Ford was one of just six senators to vote against extending those protections to women's college athletics. The bill passed 42-6. In 2023, Ford also voted against legislation [banning gender-transition procedures for minors](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fdtijuy-hhlljjcji-t/). The bill passed the Senate 36-12 and ultimately became law. Hoosier parents will remember those votes. Beau Bayh looked at that record and called it worth being proud of. So what does that say about his judgment? Either he agrees with Ford's votes, or he's willing to overlook them. Neither is the judgment Hoosiers want in a Secretary of State. He can't tell Hoosier parents he's on their side after welcoming the man who voted against them onto his team. He can't have it both ways."Fairness for our daughters isn't negotiable, and it isn't a nonissue," said Indiana Republican Party Chairwoman Lana Keesling. "Who you're proud to stand beside tells Hoosiers everything about your judgment, and Beau Bayh is proud to stand beside someone who voted against that fairness. Hoosiers deserve a Secretary of State who shares their values and says the same thing no matter who's in the room. Max Engling is that candidate."Max Engling, the Republican nominee for Secretary of State, has said plainly that men should not play in women's sports. It is not a position he has to be asked about twice. Beau Bayh, by contrast, called the question a nonissue and then celebrated the man who voted against women. Hoosiers are still waiting on a straight answer.### [](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fdtijuy-hhlljjcji-i/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fdtijuy-hhlljjcji-d/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fdtijuy-hhlljjcji-h/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fdtijuy-hhlljjcji-k/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fdtijuy-hhlljjcji-u/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fdtijuy-hhlljjcji-p/) ** PAID FOR BY THE INDIANA REPUBLICAN STATE COMMITTEE. ****NOT AUTHORIZED BY ANY CANDIDATE OR CANDIDATE'S COMMITTEE. ****WWW.INDIANA.GOP.** | Indiana Republican State Committee 101 W. We don’t have that kind of special interest money to fuel our get-out-the-vote efforts. What we have is y’all. Folks, I’ve been the underdog before. I lost my first state Senate race by 20 points. I came back, won that seat, and later flipped the chamber blue. This race is a dead heat, and I know what it takes to close a gap like this, but I can’t do it alone. Every dollar you give right now helps us reach voters while they’re casting their ballots. Thank you so much, Aaron

We have less than two weeks left to beat John Sununu and help take back the United States Senate.
Last Saturday in Exeter, we gathered with Governor Gavin Newsom, Senator Maggie Hassan, Cinde Warmington, Stefany Shaheen, and a room full of Granite Staters who are ready to finish this race strong.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fd95e8d9-ce8e-4566-9d12-3652a050475f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The people who will power us over the finish line are the ones who filled that room along with those knocking doors, making calls, and talking to their neighbors every day. This campaign was built by grassroots supporters from New Hampshire and across the country, and all of you will decide this race in these final 12 days.
Donald Trump, Elon Musk, and a network of special interest donors have spent over $64 million trying to buy this seat for John Sununu. They're betting that their millions can drown out the voices of the people of New Hampshire. We're betting on you.
**The other side has millions in outside spending. We have you.**
**[Will you chip in $15 today to help us win New Hampshire and flip the Senate in 12 days?](https://substack.com/redirect/fd95e8d9-ce8e-4566-9d12-3652a050475f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ DONATE](https://substack.com/redirect/fd95e8d9-ce8e-4566-9d12-3652a050475f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
_If you couldn 't be there on Saturday, here's the full transcript of my remarks:_
* * *
Good afternoon, Exeter.
Thanks, everyone, for joining this great event today. I want to thank Senator Hassan for your introduction and your comments, and most importantly, for the leadership that you're providing for the people of New Hampshire right now.
This is not a time to stand down. It's a time to stand up. And if you've watched Maggie Hassan in action over the last couple of years in Washington, she is standing up for the people of New Hampshire every day. Thank you for your leadership.
And what a great day when we can join our next Congresswoman, Stefany Shaheen, and our next Governor, Cinde Warmington. Thank you for being out here, guys. I know it's been a long day.
It's another No Kings Day. Happy No Kings Day, everyone.
This is the original No Kings state. You heard a little bit about the history right here in Exeter 250 years ago when we inked independence into the fabric of who we are as Granite Staters. We didn't stand for kings then, and we're not about to start doing that in 2026, are we?
I've got members of my family here. My amazing mom and my husband Vann are here. This is an all-hands-on-deck team effort. We need everyone under the tent.
This week we announced a list of endorsers for our campaign who are putting country over party. We are building a big tent, because it's not just about bringing together progressives and moderate Democrats. It's about bringing together independents and Republicans who are sick and tired of what's going on in this nation, who know that this is not as good as it gets for the United States of America.
**Together we can write a chapter and build a future that is fairer and freer for every Granite Stater, and everyone has a stake in that future.**
We're really proud of the support that we are building, and it includes all of you from every single corner of this state.
We've got to get out there and do the work these next 17 days, because everything is on the line. This is the most important midterm election of our lifetime, because we have a government and a reckless, incompetent president who is out of control.
You can count on one hand the number of Republicans that are actually standing up and doing something about it. That caucus of capitulation and cowardice has far too many members in Washington, D.C. right now. And despite some showing occasional concern, we can't send a Senator from New Hampshire who is going to capitulate and cower to Donald Trump. We need someone who's going to put the people of this state first.
John Sununu has said as much. He says that this race is "important to Donald Trump's agenda" and to protecting the successes of the Trump Administration. Now I don't know what those successes are. Do you?
Is it $4.50 gas? Is it record diesel costs? Is it the $1,000 that you just put in your home heating oil tank? Is it the fact that tens of thousands of Granite Staters are losing health care? Is it the tariffs that are hammering our small businesses? What are those successes?
John Sununu sounds a lot like Trump, who proclaims this to be a golden age for America. Are you buying that? The people of New Hampshire aren't buying it.
It might be a golden age if you're Don Jr. and a Russian oligarch is paying for your wedding reception. It might be a golden age if you're the pool guy who just got a no-bid contract to do the reflecting pool. It might be a golden age if you're getting special treatment and you're part of the Epstein class. And it might be a golden age if you're Donald Trump himself, who's $2.2 billion richer than when he came into the White House in January of last year.
The corruption is out in the open right now, and people like John Sununu are turning a blind eye to it. They're sidling up to Donald Trump on all the policies that are making life worse: the way our economy is being rigged for those at the top and the way our political system is being flooded with all this out-of-state money because they think that their millions are more powerful than your voice.
**But here in New Hampshire, we 're going to say something pretty profound this year: Our votes are not for sale.**
This is still the Live Free or Die state, and we have the power in our own hands to decide what comes next in this country.
We get to decide that we're not just going to blindly follow Donald Trump's agenda. We get to stand up and fight for people in New Hampshire who deserve a better future. We get to fight to make sure we're delivering health care as a right, and not a privilege, to every Granite Stater. We're fighting hard to get big money out of our political system, end partisan gerrymandering, and put the power of our democracy in your hands.
We have the power to determine how we protect our air and our water and act to protect this planet and take action on climate change. We have the power to bring down costs and make sure that there's opportunity for families who are struggling and sturdy rungs on the ladder of opportunity for future generations.
We have the power to build a strong system of public education and take on those that are siphoning money out of our public schools. We have the power to protect the personal freedoms of everyone, especially women who have been subject to draconian laws all across this country that are taking away their right to choose. We can restore _Roe v. Wade_ if we reassert our political power this year.
There's so much that we can accomplish.
I had two debates this week with John Sununu. In one of them, he said that he wasn't going to tell you what his plans were for Social Security because he was afraid he was going to get attacked in the campaign for them. Probably means he wants to cut benefits, right? Probably means he would entertain cutting benefits or raising the retirement age. But I have to tell you this: I am fighting to preserve Social Security and make sure that it's there for today's seniors and tomorrow's retirees.
This election is about how we muster the courage we need to stand up to a broken presidency, how we stand up to the billionaire class and the corporate special interests that are calling all the shots in Washington, D.C. right now, and how we write that next chapter for the future of New Hampshire and for this nation.
It's about turning the page on Trump and turning the page on the broken politics of the past that are reflected by John Sununu.
I don't have to remind you all that he was our Senator before. Many of you remember that. It didn't end well for New Hampshire. He was down the line for George W. Bush. He supported forever wars. He supported massive tax breaks to the super-wealthy and the biggest corporations that added trillions of dollars to our debt. He supported a $700 billion bailout of Wall Street while Main Street got screwed during the housing crisis. He voted to put anti-choice judges on the bench who overturned _Roe v. Wade_.
We've seen the movie before. We know the sequel is always worse. Why would we walk into the theater again and buy a ticket to see the show?
We've got to turn the page on John Sununu and the broken politics of the past, because this is about what comes next. We need a new generation of leadership in the United States Senate, and I'm fighting to be that Senator from New Hampshire.
These guys are flooding the zone with their dark money. We see it every day. It's on all of your screens, and it's coming from Donald Trump's super PAC, from Elon Musk, from the Koch network, literally spending over $64 million already and counting on this race.
But we've got something pretty profound to talk about here. It's a message about the future. It's a message about hope. It's a message about inclusion. It's a message about a fair economy. And we're going to work hard the next 17 days to deliver that message.
We need your help to get it out. So sign up for a canvass shift, make some phone calls, talk to your neighbors about the stakes in this election.
We have come so far over the last year and a half, at a moment where Trump wasn't counting on this sort of response from the American public. He thought we would be so overwhelmed that we would back off of our responsibilities as citizens, that we would just relinquish our vote, our power to speak out and push back.
This is a time not to fold. It's time to continue to fight and do what you have done on No Kings Day, at the protest in Merrimack, New Hampshire, to stop that ICE facility from being built, and in special elections where we've been picking up steam in towns and cities across New Hampshire. We are on the march. We have to sustain this effort over the next 17 days to get the kind of representation that we deserve in Washington, D.C.
This is a tough fight, but we can absolutely win it. Let's continue to link arms. Let's continue to work hard.
At the beginning of Trump 2.0, there were a lot of Democrats saying, "Well just ride it out, and you'll have a good midterm in a couple of years." That doesn't work for people who are being harmed by the policies of this government. It doesn't work for our federal workforce that is being drummed out of service with the DOGE cuts. It doesn't work for New Hampshire families who are losing access to health care. It doesn't work for people who care about the strength of American democracy.
Governor Newsom showed us how to stand up and fight back, not with one hand tied behind our back, but by trying to find every point of leverage that we have to make the case and to hold the line for democracy and Americans who are counting on us.
We've got to continue to muster that courage over the next 17 days. If we follow that example, we're going to win here. We're going to elect candidates up and down the ticket. We're going to turn New Hampshire blue from top to bottom, and we're going to flip the majorities, not just in Concord, but in the House and Senate in Washington and begin to unwind the damage that's been caused to our democracy.
Let's get out there and do it. Let's keep fighting. Let's win this. Let's deliver the kind of future that New Hampshire deserves.
I'd be honored to be your Senator. Let's work to make it happen.
Thank you so much. Thanks for being here.

name: Roy Cooper
subject: Two Carolinas, one Senate majority
body:
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1724&source=&t=1&akid=4846%2E124072%2E1XayQh) | | | |
---
Peter, I’m reaching out with an urgent request.
Just south of us, Annie Andrews is running for U.S. Senate in South Carolina, and she needs our help.
This is a tough seat. South Carolina hasn’t elected a Democrat to the Senate in over 25 years. But Annie is proof that the tide is turning. The polls are tightening, and she’s holding strong against Trump’s hand-picked MAGA candidate.
[**_If that’s all you need to hear and you’re ready to help make history in South Carolina, please chip in $5 to our campaign and Annie Andrews’ campaign today._](https://act.roycooper.com/go/20003?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1724&amount=5&t=8&akid=4846%2E124072%2E1XayQh)**
Annie knows hard work. She’s a pediatrician with more than 20 years of service to her community. In the exam room, she saw firsthand how the failures of our health care system and the policies coming out of Washington DC hurt families.
She’s also a mom of three who worries about what more chaos and corruption will mean for her state. So she’s stepping up to take that fight to Washington.
Like mine, Annie’s campaign is powered by grassroots supporters chipping in what they can, when they can. She’s fighting back against constant attacks from Trump and millions of dollars from the GOP trying to drown out her campaign. All to prop up an opponent who got into this race only after Trump asked her to.
Annie is a proven fighter who has worked hard for her community and is ready to continue leading the charge in Washington. That’s the kind of partner I want in the U.S. Senate.
What happens in South Carolina will affect the entire country. [**_If you’re ready to see two Carolina Democrats working together in Washington, please split a $5 donation between our campaign and Annie Andrews’ campaign today._](https://act.roycooper.com/go/20003?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1724&amount=5&t=9&akid=4846%2E124072%2E1XayQh)**

Roy

Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
subject: The destination
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
Thank you for everything you've done to support me and our fight.
#
First and foremost, I want to thank you for the support you've given me throughout my time in Congress. Because of the generosity of millions of donors and volunteers over the years, not only have we overcome millions in spending trying to defeat us, but we've done so much more.
The Fight Oligarchy Tour, the travel to support progressive candidates across the country, the contributions we've given to candidates and worthy organizations, the organizers we've hired and then some...
There's a piece of your support in everything we've done in the fight for our shared values.
Thank you.
And while I truly wish I did not have to ask you to donate to support our work today, that is what I have to do.
Because while we have done everything we can to help flip the House and Senate with candidates you can believe in, Election Day is just a point in the journey -- it is not the destination.
The destination is a new world, a better country -- one that prioritizes the dignity of all people. And that dignity looks like living wages; It looks like stable housing; It looks like guaranteed healthcare and respect for all of our differences, no matter who we are or where we come from.
That is what I am working toward every day.
But that work also requires resources.
That is why I am asking.
[Can you please make a contribution to support our work today? Our average donation is around $16. Many give more. Many give less. All that matters is the number of people chipping in. The rest will take care of itself.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-26-q4.h3BeQC&refcode=em20261022-12474-P_FND_EGR_MIS&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=4&akid=12474%2E2526796%2Eg84EOd)

Thank you for everything you've done to support me and our fight.
In solidarity,
Alexandria
**[Contribute Now](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-26-q4.h3BeQC&refcode=em20261022-12474-P_FND_EGR_MIS&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=6&akid=12474%2E2526796%2Eg84EOd)**

name: Adam Schiff
subject: Either Trump or Musk is lying
disclaimer_text: Paid for and authorized by Schiff for Senate
body:
| Either the President of the United States or the world’s richest man is lying about a decision that put Ukrainian lives at risk.
---
[](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/8022?amount=10&t=1&refcode=aschiff_email_102226_starlink&akid=10861%2E5257348%2EwtIcgP)
Either the President of the United States or the world’s richest man is lying about a decision that put Ukrainian lives at risk. Here is what the Wall Street Journal just reported: On Oct. 14, Elon Musk capped the speeds at which Ukraine’s hardware could connect to a military-grade version of Starlink, leaving some of their offensive and interceptor drones virtually useless as Russian missiles were flying. President Zelenskyy warned that Ukrainians might die as a result. The speed cap came amid a fight both men have been having with Ukraine. Elon Musk and Donald Trump have each voiced anger at Ukraine for striking Russian diesel refineries, and Trump blames those strikes for high energy prices. All while cozying up to Putin. The two spoke about the slowdown soon after it became public, and one source says they discussed it before Musk acted. SpaceX then reportedly called the White House to line up a story that the two had coordinated ahead of time. Now Musk says any limits are ultimately the president’s call. Trump says he didn’t limit anything and doesn’t believe Musk did either. _I spent years as a federal prosecutor, and I know what it looks like when two witnesses each point away from themselves. Both accounts cannot be true, and the evidence belongs on the record, under oath. For the American people to hear._ A decision with life-and-death consequences for an ally at war — one that two men now decline to own — should be made in our country’s interest, and never on one man’s personal whim. That’s why the Senate must open a full investigation and why Musk must be compelled to testify. But compelling anyone takes subpoena power, and that means we have to win the Senate majority, the one check on his power he cannot fire. **[If you're with me, add your name in support of a full Senate investigation into Elon Musk, Starlink, and this administration's betrayal of Ukraine.](https://act.adamschiff.com/signup/aschiff_email_102226_starlink/?t=10&refcode=aschiff_email_102226_starlink&akid=10861%2E5257348%2EwtIcgP)** | | [ADD YOUR NAME→](https://act.adamschiff.com/signup/aschiff_email_102226_starlink/?t=11&refcode=aschiff_email_102226_starlink&akid=10861%2E5257348%2EwtIcgP)

Last night, I faced Sen. Marshall on the debate stage. The contrast could not have been clearer.
While Marshall was defending his Medicaid cuts and extreme, abusive medical debt collection practices, I made it clear that I will be a champion for Kansans in the Senate, not a spokesperson for just a party or a president.
I asked Kansans a simple question: _Are you happy with how things are in Washington?_ Because what I’ve heard from Kansans is that sky-high prices are hurting folks every single day. Kansans see the cruelty in how our leaders treat our fellow human beings — and they know that that’s not who we are.
**It’s time for something different.** This grassroots movement is gearing up to retire Sen. Marshall once and for all and end the chaos and corruption in Washington.

name: Kristan Hawkins
subject: They're getting doors slammed in their faces
body:
Two weeks until Election Day. Our student canvassers need to know you have their backs.

*|MC_PREVIEW_TEXT|* | | |
---
| | [](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0L-K3DAQx_Gnkbs11siW7woVgWW7S5vSzEojrTj9QxpfyNsHh-QF0kzzheHD78fH8YExxRK-YybT2R99HPyiX50CMccSXK19jIQ5kztgAX2Tyw3gQMvxi44VJ2ecdSjtREbu76D1tqxyehklUdlt2_zT2ze9u402qzYlnb8OwBTN9U8uAHJRi3qbcfc7qSfsK0m7wVOsCybqPHdq5zNFi4VxfPraLc225imZF3MbQn0T8BDwGGTPTvPg01Hh4WtP0dNFrWWuPQh4NLxZ7NTQfmIg0EI9RrdC3Sm3LkDnEaIT6n7B5HtDAfrkfFjMDWMoV_mL_ldqYSos1L2zn7px7WdMKQ69i3UJGWP6Q-X_XPfLwO8AAAD___fci3A)

Dear Pro-Life Friend,

Our volunteer student canvassers have been through the wringer these past couple of months.

Doors get slammed in their faces. They get shouted off stoops. And sometimes, even worse things happen.

So, I’ve told every one of our canvassers to prepare for anything over the next two weeks.

Pro-Life Friend, our student canvassers know what’s on the line.

They know if abortion-loving leftists seize power in November, it will be a death sentence to millions more innocent preborn babies.

And they know the job’s not done yet.

But right now, they could use a little moral boost heading into the final weeks before Election Day on Tuesday, November 3rd.

[That’s why I’m hoping you’ll prayerfully consider sending a Care Package to one of our door-to-door canvassers](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0L-K3DAQx_Gnkbs11siW7woVgWW7S5vSzEojrTj9QxpfyNsHh-QF0kzzheHD78fH8YExxRK-YybT2R99HPyiX50CMccSXK19jIQ5kztgAX2Tyw3gQMvxi44VJ2ecdSjtREbu76D1tqxyehklUdlt2_zT2ze9u402qzYlnb8OwBTN9U8uAHJRi3qbcfc7qSfsK0m7wVOsCybqPHdq5zNFi4VxfPraLc225imZF3MbQn0T8BDwGGTPTvPg01Hh4WtP0dNFrWWuPQh4NLxZ7NTQfmIg0EI9RrdC3Sm3LkDnEaIT6n7B5HtDAfrkfFjMDWMoV_mL_ldqYSos1L2zn7px7WdMKQ69i3UJGWP6Q-X_XPfLwO8AAAD___fci3A)**.**

My name is Kristan Hawkins, and I’m the President of Students for Life Action. You can think of us as the grassroots arm of the Pro-Life Movement.

These young women and men will be on their feet for hours, walking door to door. And knowing pro-lifers like you have their backs will help keep them going.

Of course, I could tell our door knockers to go home.

I could focus on running expensive TV ads instead.

But studies show that face-to-face conversations move voters more than any TV ad ever could. And the effect doesn’t disappear after one election.

**Voters who talk to one of our students in person are more likely to show up and vote again in the next election, too.**

And, it costs us less than $3 for every door we knock.

This is the on-the-ground grassroots campaigning that’s needed to turn out every pro-life voter.

Last cycle, this approach worked.
**> >> In Oklahoma,** our canvassers knocked 633 doors, made 26,931 phone calls, and sent 26,078 texts exposing two pro-abortion state senators who killed our legislation to stop chemical abortion pill trafficking. Voters threw them out.

**> >> In South Carolina,** we knocked 2,572 doors and made 51,371 calls exposing three pro-abortion Republican senators who killed our “Life at Conception Act.” They lost too.

**> >> In North Carolina,** 1,052 doors and 52,554 texts helped four pro-life candidates win their primaries.
The Abortion Lobby would love nothing more than for our students to give up and go home during this final stretch.

It’s true they have the money, the media, and the institutions.

But what they don’t have is thousands of young pro-lifers willing to knock on a stranger’s door, get yelled at, sometimes get hit with worse than words, and still go knock on the next door.

That grit and determination is what wins elections.

[So, will you please make your most generous contribution today to keep our canvassers in the field through the two most important weeks of this election season](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0L-K3DAQx_Gnkbs11siW7woVgWW7S5vSzEojrTj9QxpfyNsHh-QF0kzzheHD78fH8YExxRK-YybT2R99HPyiX50CMccSXK19jIQ5kztgAX2Tyw3gQMvxi44VJ2ecdSjtREbu76D1tqxyehklUdlt2_zT2ze9u402qzYlnb8OwBTN9U8uAHJRi3qbcfc7qSfsK0m7wVOsCybqPHdq5zNFi4VxfPraLc225imZF3MbQn0T8BDwGGTPTvPg01Hh4WtP0dNFrWWuPQh4NLxZ7NTQfmIg0EI9RrdC3Sm3LkDnEaIT6n7B5HtDAfrkfFjMDWMoV_mL_ldqYSos1L2zn7px7WdMKQ69i3UJGWP6Q-X_XPfLwO8AAAD___fci3A)**?**
**> >> $250** fully funds a canvasser’s entire day in the field: more than 80 doors knocked, one voter conversation at a time.

**> >> $100** puts a canvasser on more than 30 doors in a key race.

**> >> $50** covers a tank of gas for a canvasser’s day of driving to and from strategic locations.

**> >> $25** pays for a canvasser’s meals for a day in the field.

**> >> $10** puts our pro-life message on more than three doors.
Pro-Life Friend, door knocking has been our key to beating both the Abortion Lobby and the D.C. consultant class for years.

You see, they like wasting their donors’ money on flashy, expensive cable TV ads because it lines their pockets.

Meanwhile, real people having real conversations are what actually move voters in November. That’s how we helped 119 pro-life legislators WIN in 2024!

So, please let our dedicated student activists know you care about them and appreciate the hard work they’re doing for the entire pro-life movement.

[Will you please send a Care Package to one of our canvassers right now](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0L-K3DAQx_Gnkbs11siW7woVgWW7S5vSzEojrTj9QxpfyNsHh-QF0kzzheHD78fH8YExxRK-YybT2R99HPyiX50CMccSXK19jIQ5kztgAX2Tyw3gQMvxi44VJ2ecdSjtREbu76D1tqxyehklUdlt2_zT2ze9u402qzYlnb8OwBTN9U8uAHJRi3qbcfc7qSfsK0m7wVOsCybqPHdq5zNFi4VxfPraLc225imZF3MbQn0T8BDwGGTPTvPg01Hh4WtP0dNFrWWuPQh4NLxZ7NTQfmIg0EI9RrdC3Sm3LkDnEaIT6n7B5HtDAfrkfFjMDWMoV_mL_ldqYSos1L2zn7px7WdMKQ69i3UJGWP6Q-X_XPfLwO8AAAD___fci3A)**?**

For Life,

Kristan Hawkins
President, Students for Life Action

P.S. – Election Day is Tuesday, November 3rd, and our canvassers will be knocking on doors right up to the finish line. [Please help keep them in the field with a Care Package Gift of $25 or more today](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0L-K3DAQx_Gnkbs11siW7woVgWW7S5vSzEojrTj9QxpfyNsHh-QF0kzzheHD78fH8YExxRK-YybT2R99HPyiX50CMccSXK19jIQ5kztgAX2Tyw3gQMvxi44VJ2ecdSjtREbu76D1tqxyehklUdlt2_zT2ze9u402qzYlnb8OwBTN9U8uAHJRi3qbcfc7qSfsK0m7wVOsCybqPHdq5zNFi4VxfPraLc225imZF3MbQn0T8BDwGGTPTvPg01Hh4WtP0dNFrWWuPQh4NLxZ7NTQfmIg0EI9RrdC3Sm3LkDnEaIT6n7B5HtDAfrkfFjMDWMoV_mL_ldqYSos1L2zn7px7WdMKQ69i3UJGWP6Q-X_XPfLwO8AAAD___fci3A)**.** _Students for Life Action is a non-profit, tax-exempt advocacy organization under section 501(c)(4) of the IRC. Contributions or gifts to Students for Life Action are not tax deductible for IRS purposes; they do, however, avoid recognition of gain on appreciated assets. Students for Life Action’s mailing address is 600 Princess Anne St #7667, Fredericksburg, VA 22401. Any donations raised above or short of the goal will be used in the next area of greatest need towards our mission, as determined by the organization._

Dear Peter, In America, the people choose their government. And the people deserve to know their choices have been accurately recorded and counted. Elections must be conducted according to the law, with transparency and reliable records to prove the results. As another national election approaches, questions about public confidence remain. At Unite4Freedom, our optimism is grounded in something tangible:**we understand the problem, we have a strategy, and we are making progress.** In addition to **State Scorecards in 35 states** and **Vote Tampering Reports in 10 states** , consider what we've accomplished this year:
* Volunteers used Unite4Freedom's data analysis to file administrative complaints in 5 states, pursue formal hearings concerning compliance with federal election requirements and citizens' right to be heard, and achieve **on-the-record hearings in Missouri, Colorado, and Illinois.**
* Unite4Freedom issued **formal notices to 30 states** about potential violations of federal voter registration requirements. We maintain that the states' responses have not fully addressed or reconciled those concerns, providing **a basis for further legal action.**
* Unite4Freedom issued **preservation notices to 35 states** ahead of election-record retention deadlines, requesting that records be preserved and notifying officials of potential civil litigation if violations are not corrected.
* Our Pennsylvania lawsuit **survived a motion to dismiss** , allowing us to continue pursuing our claims in court. We are preparing additional federal litigation based on our previously listed complaints and analysis.

**Our work doesn't end on Election Day.** These accomplishments are part of a long-term strategy to document concerns, obtain on-the-record review, and pursue accountability through established legal processes. Meaningful reform takes time. clean_body: In America, the people choose their government. | Dear Peter, In America, the people choose their government. And the people deserve to know their choices have been accurately recorded and counted. Elections must be conducted according to the law, with transparency and reliable records to prove the results. As another national election approaches, questions about public confidence remain. At Unite4Freedom, our optimism is grounded in something tangible:we understand the problem, we have a strategy, and we are making progress. In addition to State Scorecards in 35 states and Vote Tampering Reports in 10 states , consider what we've accomplished this year: Volunteers used Unite4Freedom's data analysis to file administrative complaints in 5 states, pursue formal hearings concerning compliance with federal election requirements and citizens' right to be heard, and achieve on-the-record hearings in Missouri, Colorado, and Illinois. Unite4Freedom issued formal notices to 30 states about potential violations of federal voter registration requirements. We maintain that the states' responses have not fully addressed or reconciled those concerns, providing a basis for further legal action. Unite4Freedom issued preservation notices to 35 states ahead of election-record retention deadlines, requesting that records be preserved and notifying officials of potential civil litigation if violations are not corrected. Our Pennsylvania lawsuit survived a motion to dismiss , allowing us to continue pursuing our claims in court. We are preparing additional federal litigation based on our previously listed complaints and analysis. Our work doesn't end on Election Day. These accomplishments are part of a long-term strategy to document concerns, obtain on-the-record review, and pursue accountability through established legal processes. Meaningful reform takes time. Unite4Freedom remains committed to examining election records, seeking answers, and pursuing legal remedies beyond this election. body:
We were almost there. We can still win this.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter, I want to be straight with you, because you’ve earned that.
Back in April, I was down almost 7 points to Greg Abbott in the polling average. Political insiders wrote this race off. Then you showed up: you chipped in, spread the word, and proved that people all over the country believe Texas can be taken back. **By October 7, we had cut that gap to just 1.3 points.**
I know a lot of you saw that number and felt what I felt: _we can actually do this._
But since then, the polls have moved in the wrong direction. Today, the average has me trailing Abbott by 2.4 points.
Here’s what I need you to hear:**2.4 points is not a lost race.** This is one of the most competitive governor’s races in the country, and it will be decided by turnout, by organizing, and by what we do in these final days.

Two weeks ago, we were closer to beating Greg Abbott than anyone thought possible. If we let up now, we could lose this race by a margin we could have closed. [**I need you in this fight with me. Can you chip in $15 today to help us get back to where we were and finish the job?**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261022_1_pollslipped.7O9mka&refcode=emrefcode%3Dem20261022-mailing_id&amount=15&t=2&akid=2500%2E299639%2E1HxzFv)
Early voting is already underway, and every dollar we raise right now goes straight into reaching the voters who will decide this thing. We can’t get comfortable. Not for a single day. **We have to make sure every voter hears the truth about Greg Abbott before they cast their ballot.**
Here’s just one example: yesterday, a watchdog investigation found that Abbott’s much-hyped “pause” on data center permits was never a pause at all. Dozens of projects kept moving forward. That’s Greg Abbott: a press release for voters, business as usual for his corporate allies.
_**Your donation could be the difference between winning and losing.**_ It could decide whether Texas gets four more years of Greg Abbott’s corruption or whether we take Texas back.
I’ve never needed your support more. [**Will you chip in $15 now so we can close this 2.4-point gap before Election Day?**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1374?c0=em_ms_gh_20261022_1_pollslipped.cBTQVO&refcode=em20261022-2500&t=4&akid=2500%2E299639%2E1HxzFv)
[Donate »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20261022_1_pollslipped.Yhe3Q5&refcode=em20261022-2500&t=23&akid=2500%2E299639%2E1HxzFv)
We closed a 7-point gap once already. Two points is within reach, but it’s now or never, and I need you with me today.
Thank you,
Gina

## Van Zandt Deputy Killed in Shootout
Gunfire from a home south of Canton killed a Van Zandt County sheriff's deputy and wounded a Canton police officer Tuesday night as they [tried to arrest a man](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLEOmzAURb_GbEb2CzEweOjClq4d0cN-BCuOjfADkn59RfsJ3a50paOj8-sxPjDEkJ4_8U2WP3MeE50lEjNtI9MHy4xpwpTIIxMlfBKWMoICI7WSACM6DgeNDVbeTsr3uiKr2x6MMX3XV4ttjYEOtOmcQ2_mSfVN204Om6mHuVW3KtgLpxWA1uqmutrNzb3plLl3k7tj14tGkQ-ct5oX-icVv_mgrXb5XUW7MK9F3H4IGAQM53nWL97oOgUMF1vAoNW1tYDhwCR_Y_IsXd4Tf6WndeevfIUYyUuHiXOSeZ6Do00u-8ayLDlz3lmWvazkWHpCL2CoNuvXM8QYimlFo55vDPGvFP9vzMPCnwAAAP__poeKGg) wanted for aggravated assault and assaulting a peace officer. Deputies were helping Canton police serve the warrants on state Highway 198 when [shots came from inside](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGSozAQRL8GMlHSGGQUKLiEzJdeSA3SYHQrSy40gL1fv8XuJ2zWQVfX6_fvNt4wxJDuf_FBll9zHhMdJRIzrSPTC8uMacKUyCMTJbwTljKCBC2UFAAjOg47jS3W3k7SG1WTVVcDWmvTm3qxymlwUyelUlLJFkw_qU57R94Aor7UwZ5zSgIoJS-yb9zcdm0vdddPrsPeVK0kHzivDS_0AxXfeae1cflRR7swP0t1-VPBUMFwHEcz51d7HjkLFQxnrGDYMYlPTJ6Fy1vit_D03PgtPkKM5IXDxDmJPM_B0SpC-r-t5EVZcua8cb1a_zxCjKHoa9XK-wND_Cbg35rbLXwFAAD__w6YheQ) the house around 10:22 p.m. Officers returned fire, and the suspect was found dead inside from a gunshot wound. The deputy's brother [identified him as Adam Sherifi](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLHSmzAQhJ8GOnmkA4RUqEhD96dNyRzSCWsiCw86g52nz5A8wl_e3O7Ot_vra_7ClFNZf-KDHL_jNhc6ayZm2memN9aIZcFSKCATFVwJa51BghZKCoAZPaeD5h7b4BYZrGrJqdGC1toa295dHGE00UY5AtAQBuujCnHs9OLJgrJtcleckgBKyU6am4_90BupB7P4AY1tekkh8bbf-E7_ofJnO2i_-e3RZndnftam-9HA1MB0nuftKnFSZXspGphw5-QzNTBdnwYmv6fHdR5YxB8sgYXfXoU_ItDzxR9RX_VJnsXvlDMFsb5KTDsJevs7lvVyDlKJzuqFKAwiWGVFD70URmoUGNRoQvTdYPp2d-F5ppxT1WPTy_WBKf8D5-8Ofjj4GwAA__9BrZUN), who leaves behind a wife and young children. A memorial now stands outside the sheriff's office. The wounded officer was [flown to Plano for surgery](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2ynDAQhE8jMlFC_CpQ4ITsOXVIDdIIxtZKFJqFt7d37foIzrv66_5-fS1fQJHS9hMeaPk75CXhXSIy47kwfkMJkFZICT0wYoINoZRFKz3IRkmtF3BMFy4dVN6uypumQtuMRg_DYCZT7dYMyo0QTB_C2CpA064dmFH3rlfetK4i-65rlNZNo1o11S50fTepoZ9W18NkRKfQE-ez5h3_jYqvfOFZu_yoot2ZjyLaH0LPQs_3fdcXxIgvh4lPiO-U0PP7mNCzx-PJL_mHYkQvjxzJocwhkMNTUvr9PNFLShKhsPzAZNlzZkqbvIl3WZ7lQMdCz9Vp_XFTjFSGUXRqewB9aBX_r8vL6r8BAAD__3XGjOE) on a gunshot wound to his right arm and is in stable condition. The Texas Rangers are investigating, and officials haven't named the officer or the suspect.
## Transgender Mailers Traced to Wyoming
Mailers offering transgender resources to Texas students, addressed to the kids instead of their parents, came from [a company registered in Wyoming](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDFygzAQRU8DnZhFFjIqVKShc9qUzCItoBlZ8kgb49w-g3OEdFvsvPf__7rNNwwxpO0T72T5teY50VEjMVOZmV5YV0wLpkQemSjhRljrLEFq0YOQckbH4UmzwtbbBbzpW7L91UittRlNu1uEBbBXsIC6GPJmADJKK3LrCAvh2gZ74nqQsu_hAmPnVjWoEfQwLm7A0TQKyAfOpeOd_kLFn_yk0rl8b6PdmR-1uXw0cmrkdBxHt-aXOoucD42czrOR0yPHwMFhFHcMkUoVXDDVjZKnIgrV_F0cVeH2EH2hJFIuvIu3sS3WP44QY6j62ijYTsTbz__d7WnlbwAAAP__AVeGKA) on Sept. 2 whose owners aren't public. The envelopes started arriving as early voting opened, addressed to "Students Of The [Last Name] Family." Inside is a guide on student legal rights, emancipation, and finding support outside the family. The envelope's [return address doesn't exist](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuwyAURb8Gb1jw4hA8MHTxlq4drWd4tlEJjuAlTv--cvoJ3a50pKOj-3UdrxhTzMsn3sjxa97GTHtNxExlZHphnTFPmDMFZKKMC2GtIygwUisJMKLn-KSxwya4SYVeN-T0pQdjTG_7ZnXBBm99fwrezzMao2yPCqYOw0zWdNhEd-i0AtBanZRt_dydO6vM2U7-jLYXnaIQeSstr_QXlX62J5XWb7cmuZX5XsXpQ8AgYNj3vf2e-HVAAcPhFjBodWwtYHgLZOVHoMxVLsQc8yK5YK4L5UBFFqrbo3iSN4yJSpX7ugkYmuLCfY8pxWouolPLgd8N_N_vng5-AwAA___xe4UF). A CALL TO ACTION
---
|
---
This won't be a year when we can sit back and expect everyone else to do the work. If you want to change the direction of the country, you have to get into the game. If you can help us with any of these efforts, drop us a note, and we will be in touch. Here is what you can do to help us win in November:
---
|
---
Events: We're a grassroots campaign, so we need to meet people face-to-face. If you're having a fall festival, food truck event, flea market, farmers market, or art fair, let us know.
---
| |
---
| Sign Waving: Gather some friends and wave signs on any busy streetcorner, we can get you more signs and t-shirts.
---
| |
---
| Canvassing: We need volunteers to help organize canvassing or work with other candidates to coordinate efforts. We can provide lists of addresses for potential swing voters and as many push cards as you want.
---
| |
---
| Phone banking: If your county already does phone banking, we can team with you to include our campaign in your message.
---
| |
---
| Host an event: We want to meet your friends.

| |
---
| Make a plan to vote: Tell everyone you know to vote, offer rides to the polls, THEN VOTE.

# One Last Thought Until Next Week
---
| | |
---
Hey everybody,
Since we started this campaign back in the summer of 2025, we've said the election would hinge on two groups: Independents and swayable Republicans.
We've been talking to independent, swing voters for months. They're tired of the lack of real policies, and they're thrilled to see a Democrat fighting for this district. We've often heard that people are going to the polls for the first time in a long time because we're contesting so many races.
Well, we're now beginning to hear from the second group, swayable Republicans. In the last few weeks, I've had many discussions where I heard the phrase, "Well, I've never voted for a Democrat before, but..." The next phrase is usually, "I've been following you on social media," or, "A friend told me about you," or, "I've seen your name all over the place, so I wanted to see what you're all about."
This hasn't been one or two people. It's every time we do a public event. The whole vibe of the campaign has shifted in the last six weeks. We must be bold, and we have to be brave. For the good of this district, we need to tell people what we believe. I know it's hard to be a blue dot in a red state, but I promise you, you're not alone, and if you step up, people will respond.
So get that yard sign out; wear that t-shirt in public; take advantage of it when your neighbor says, "What do you think about this election?"
The general election is 14 days away.
Be well. We'll talk soon,

Lee

Will it benefit the people of Alabama's 3rd Congressional District? That's it. I have a great example to share, but we need a bit of background. .... | == | A Few Things to Think About | | | | | FROM THE NEWS | == "Of Alabama's 67 counties, 58 are classified as rural, and more than 40 percent of the state's population lives in rural areas. As of July 2026, 37 percent of the state's remaining rural hospitals were considered at immediate risk of closure, according to PARCA." | == Alabama's unemployment rate increased in September, even as the state added 24,300 jobs over the past year. We've often heard that people are going to the polls for the first time in a long time because we're contesting so many races. Well, we're now beginning to hear from the second group, swayable Republicans. In the last few weeks, I've had many discussions where I heard the phrase, "Well, I've never voted for a Democrat before, but..." For the good of this district, we need to tell people what we believe. I know it's hard to be a blue dot in a red state, but I promise you, you're not alone, and if you step up, people will respond. subject: My decision:
body:
The work that will decide the midterms — and whether or not we can put a stop to Trump — is happening right now, and the DNC is spearheading that effort. [](https://ak.democrats.org/go/89216?t=1&akid=10003%2E22930333%2EW0arR3)
---
Derek, this is an email from the Democratic National Committee about our work to flip Congress in 12 days. If you'd like to stop receiving emails about this contest, please [click here.](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/warren-sweepstakes-2026-opt-out/?t=2&akid=10003%2E22930333%2EW0arR3) | [](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-warren-sweepstakes-2026.k_RvmO&amount=7&refcode=em_20261022_10003_fr&t=3&akid=10003%2E22930333%2EW0arR3)
---
**Derek, will you meet me in Boston or DC?**
I’m traveling the country mobilizing voters and campaigning for fighters in battleground races, and my favorite part is meeting Democrats on the ground. That’s why, if you [**chip in $7, or any amount, to the DNC today,**](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-warren-sweepstakes-2026.k_RvmO&refcode=em_20261022_10003_fr&amount=7&t=4&akid=10003%2E22930333%2EW0arR3) you’ll be entered to win a trip, travel, and hotel included, to meet me in Boston or DC.
**[ENTER TO WIN](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-warren-sweepstakes-2026.k_RvmO&refcode=em_20261022_10003_fr&amount=7&t=5&akid=10003%2E22930333%2EW0arR3)**
Let me explain my decision: The DNC is the _only_ organization that works year-round, every year, to elect Democrats at every level. From the school board to the presidency, _every_ Democrat running for office relies on resources that the DNC provides.
**The work that will decide the midterms — and whether or not we can put a stop to Trump — is happening right now, and the DNC is spearheading that effort.** They’ve kick-started a **first-of-its-kind partisan voter registration program** in battleground districts, working to register thousands of new Democratic voters. They’ve hosted their **largest-ever training for campaign staff** , and they are working to **build a team of voter protection volunteers** that can stand up to any threats to election integrity the Trump administration may throw our way.
**Derek,_all_ of those things are only possible because of grassroots supporters like you.** Over 99% of the DNC’s contributions come from texts, ads, letters, and emails just like this one asking regular people for their support.
_That_ is why I want the opportunity to thank one of you in person. Grassroots supporters are the lifeblood of the Democratic Party, and if we take back our majorities this November, _your_ support will be the reason why.
[**So, Derek, will you chip in $7, or any amount, for a chance to meet? I would love to meet you.**](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-warren-sweepstakes-2026.k_RvmO&refcode=em_20261022_10003_fr&amount=7&t=6&akid=10003%2E22930333%2EW0arR3)

Friend,

Charlie said it best in the days leading up to President Trump's victory in 2024: _" I don't care about polls. __ __I don 't care about betting markets. __ __I don 't care about vibes. __ _ **_I care about how many ballots are in the box. _**_ __If we turnout, we win. __ _**_Do the work. " _** Do the work... Charlie knew there was no easy route to saving our country. He knew there were no shortcuts to victory. Chuck Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries each have a list.
_**At the top of both: Michigan.**_
They're not hiding it. Put Abdul El-Sayed in Mike Rogers' Senate seat. Put Christina Hines in Mike Bouchard's House seat. Do both, and they don't just win two races. They win two gavels.
Schumer gets the Senate. Jeffries gets the House. And the radical left gets the power to stop everything President Trump is doing and push through every priority they've been waiting years to pass.
**That's not speculation. That's their strategy.** And right now, they're executing it.
The two of us, together, are the difference between a Republican Congress that can govern and a Democrat Congress that cannot be stopped. Lose one of our seats, and the math gets dangerous. Lose both, and it's over.
**Here's what we're each up against:**
Abdul El-Sayed is not a Michigan candidate. He's the national progressive movement's bet on Michigan. Bernie Sanders is in his corner. He wants Medicare for All, a government takeover of your health care, and a tax-and-spend agenda that would hit Michigan families and businesses hard. He has one goal: take this Senate seat and hand it to Schumer.
Christina Hines is Hakeem Jeffries' pick to flip MI-10. House Democrats put this district on their target list, and national Democrats are lining up behind her. If she wins, she's a guaranteed vote for Speaker Jeffries and everything that comes with him.
**_[Two opponents. One coordinated plan. name: Voto Latino
subject: We need your help to turn out voters in the RGV
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Voto Latino
body:
What happens in the Rio Grande Valley this election cycle will determine whether we can flip these races or not.
#
Peter,
Early voting is officially underway across Texas, and the path to victory for major races runs straight through the Rio Grande Valley.
**We’ve identified 115,000 Latino voters across the Rio Grande Valley that we need to turn out to vote by mail and cast their ballots early in this critical election.**
These are voters who hold the power to decide the governor's race, flip a crucial U.S. Senate seat, and decide battleground congressional districts like TX-15. But right now, we’re falling behind.
**We currently only have the dedicated funds to reach 65,000 of these voters.**
That leaves a 50,000 voter gap — and in an election this close, leaving 50,000 voters out is a huge risk, and one that we don’t want to take.
When we reach voters directly with the right information and concrete voting plans, Latinos turn out in historic numbers. But if we go dark in these final days, those 50,000 voters may never hear from an organizer before the polls close.
**[Peter, will you make a donation of any amount right now to help us close this 50,000 mail-in voter gap?](https://act.votolatino.org/go/305?c0=em-ms-voto-20261022-1.B4mQkU&refcode=em20261022-700&t=1&akid=700%2E1366028%2EkPwxpp)**

Something deeply troubling is happening in America, and it’s happening faster than most people realize.

This sponsored message from Inside Scoop Politics is on behalf of Hillsdale College
| | | [](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyUkU2PmzAQhn-NuYHMQGw4cGjLplopm1WbVj0ixx5gJH8Jm-TvV5GS3nudeTTz6H3_fEwfiiz55awcDpTSZIKZ1nA3ZO64YF5xwwk4iLLmJcCkdKYbTq0qzHCAupu7Aoda9iAkF4euWIe-lnOvZlNrxWd5Ba1MfVCdaK_CNFeAgobHvZoD1MAbLiqhdd93Xau14rKThrV8j0ZlrMgnMph0CDEGS5l0qsK2FHZYc46JNV8YHBkcyc-hWsnaZJTFCs3O4KhX5SIFn8owl_OGaIIrb8HuDsu2Y80x4eLQ52_BIGtGzkUtzxxaOI2n8XN8e7swEHt2Uwr7ph9I3EKKqDP55blyaGh3rBnRKbLPoVYuKlo8a8Z_DmF-GryY4DP6zJrx18_P319P7-fv0w9Zvl8u5SudYhtMvJO1lIRkLV8eLyodXJH_r6nbAH8DAAD__0G-oJQ)

| | Dear Fellow American, Something deeply troubling is happening in America, and it’s happening faster than most people realize. Last year, New York City’s socialist mayor said he wanted to replace what he called **“the frigidity of rugged individualism” with “the warmth of collectivism.”** Then I read that a senior official in that same administration argued that private property is a tool of **oppression**. Those statements are troubling enough. But what really stopped me in my tracks was hearing a popular socialist podcaster tell his audience to **“Kill... landlords... Let the streets soak in their...****capitalist blood.****”** How on earth did ideas like these become acceptable, even helping far-Left candidates to win elections from coast to coast? If you’ve found yourself asking the same question, **[I’d like to send you a FREE copy of _Champions of Freedom: Volume 48_ on the dangers of socialism from Hillsdale College.](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyUkU2PmzAQhn-NuYHMQGw4cGjLplopm1WbVj0ixx5gJH8Jm-TvV5GS3nudeTTz6H3_fEwfiiz55awcDpTSZIKZ1nA3ZO64YF5xwwk4iLLmJcCkdKYbTq0qzHCAupu7Aoda9iAkF4euWIe-lnOvZlNrxWd5Ba1MfVCdaK_CNFeAgobHvZoD1MAbLiqhdd93Xau14rKThrV8j0ZlrMgnMph0CDEGS5l0qsK2FHZYc46JNV8YHBkcyc-hWsnaZJTFCs3O4KhX5SIFn8owl_OGaIIrb8HuDsu2Y80x4eLQ52_BIGtGzkUtzxxaOI2n8XN8e7swEHt2Uwr7ph9I3EKKqDP55blyaGh3rBnRKbLPoVYuKlo8a8Z_DmF-GryY4DP6zJrx18_P319P7-fv0w9Zvl8u5SudYhtMvJO1lIRkLV8eLyodXJH_r6nbAH8DAAD__0G-oJQ)** In this collection of speeches, Christopher Caldwell, Kimberley Strassel, John Steele Gordon and others explain where socialism came from, why it has failed everywhere it has been tried, and why it continues to attract support today. **You can claim your free e-book using the secure link below.** | | [Download Your Free Copy](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyUkU2PmzAQhn-NuYHMQGw4cGjLplopm1WbVj0ixx5gJH8Jm-TvV5GS3nudeTTz6H3_fEwfiiz55awcDpTSZIKZ1nA3ZO64YF5xwwk4iLLmJcCkdKYbTq0qzHCAupu7Aoda9iAkF4euWIe-lnOvZlNrxWd5Ba1MfVCdaK_CNFeAgobHvZoD1MAbLiqhdd93Xau14rKThrV8j0ZlrMgnMph0CDEGS5l0qsK2FHZYc46JNV8YHBkcyc-hWsnaZJTFCs3O4KhX5SIFn8owl_OGaIIrb8HuDsu2Y80x4eLQ52_BIGtGzkUtzxxaOI2n8XN8e7swEHt2Uwr7ph9I3EKKqDP55blyaGh3rBnRKbLPoVYuKlo8a8Z_DmF-GryY4DP6zJrx18_P319P7-fv0w9Zvl8u5SudYhtMvJO1lIRkLV8eLyodXJH_r6nbAH8DAAD__0G-oJQ)

subject: Making some history of our own
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Blue Amp Action
body:
|
---
_You're getting this message because you’ve supported good causes and Democratic candidates. We need your support to continue fighting for our democracy. We love having you in our network, but if you only want our most important email updates,[click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/108?t=2&akid=3637%2E259176%2ESY7Hq8) If you'd like to unsubscribe, [click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/109?t=3&akid=3637%2E259176%2ESY7Hq8)_

My heritage guides me every day, Peter.

**I am Ojibwe and a member of White Earth. My Ojibwe name, Gizhiiwewidamookwe, means “Speaks in a Loud and Clear Voice Woman.”**

It’s more than a name to me. It’s a responsibility to use my voice for all who go unheard, or get left behind.

I’ve spent my entire career fighting for kids and working families.

I helped deliver free school lunches for every kid in Minnesota.

I started the campaign to pass paid family and medical leave here in Minnesota.

I led the fight to create the first-in-the-nation Missing and Murdered Indigenous Relatives office, to address the crisis of violence against Native women and two-spirit relatives.

That means every kiddo gets a warm meal at school. That means a parent can take time to care for their sick kid without losing their job. That means all our communities are being cared for and protected.

body:
Illegal Votes, Turnout, and the Partisan Divide

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/grantdemocracy/grant-report-october-8-12775790?e=c16f400a56)
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/msYv6Jrfy3w?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a)
| | **Illegal Votes, Turnout, and the Partisan Divide** By Jeffrey Milyo, Professor of Economics, University of MissouriThe policy debate over voting rules such as voter ID, drop boxes for ballots, or vote-by-mail may be understood as disagreements about the relative importance of making it easier for eligible citizens to vote versus preventing ineligible people from doing so. The parties have staked out widely divergent positions on specific reforms, but where does the American public stand when it comes to prioritizing one goal over the other?As part of my ongoing research on election administration and with recent support from the Grant Institute, I have collected survey data on public knowledge and opinions of state election procedures over several years. A total of twelve national surveys between 2008 and 2024 asked respondents whether the more important priority for their state should be “maximizing voter turnout even if some illegal voting occurs, or minimizing illegal voting even if that reduces turnout.”Over the entire period (N>11,000), Americans chose minimizing illegal voting over increasing turnout by a margin of more than two to one. Among those identifying most strongly with the Republican Party, the ratio exceeds ten to one, and among those who lean toward neither party the ratio is about 4.6 to one. In contrast, among strong Democrats the balance tips the other way, by about 1.5 to one in favor of increasing turnout. These ratios are also stable across years, although there is some evidence of increased polarization in 2024.These findings raise the question of whether the partisan divide reflects different views of the trade-offs or cues from party leaders. In a new study with David Doherty, Conor Dowling, and Michael Miller, I address this with two survey experiments conducted in 2024. Respondents chose between two voting rules for a hypothetical town. Under one, every eligible resident voted, but so did some ineligible residents; under the other, no ineligible residents voted, but fewer eligible residents did. We randomly varied the numbers on each side, as well as which party was said to have proposed each rule.Respondents in these experiments treated an illegal vote as far weightier than a lost legal one, giving roughly as much weight to one ineligible ballot as to ten eligible citizens not voting, and Democrats and Republicans responded to these trade-offs in much the same way, although Republicans were 18 to 19 percentage points more likely to favor eliminating illegal votes. Party cues, however, had enormous effects: support for the rule that eliminated illegal voting rose by 37 to 48 percentage points when it was attributed to the respondent’s own party.These findings suggest that much of the partisan conflict over voting rules reflects signals from party leaders rather than fundamentally different values. Americans across the political spectrum place a high priority on keeping ineligible votes out of elections, which leaves more room for compromise than the current debate would suggest.Professor Milyo’s article, coauthored with David Doherty, Conor M. Dowling, and Michael G. Miller, is available [here](https://us.list-manage.com/c0Hf_wxrg3c?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a)._Professor Milyo’s work was funded in part by the Ulysses S. Grant Institute. The views expressed by the author are his own and do not necessarily reflect the views of the Institute._
