| | **Arizona** The Maricopa County Recorder’s Office [reported](https://us.list-manage.com/18ulMssKI1k?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) unauthorized overnight access to the paper trays of three ballot-on-demand printers at an early voting site at Chandler-Gilbert Community College. The office replaced the printers and sent them for forensic examination. No voters were affected.Attorney General Mayes’s office [demanded](https://us.list-manage.com/12_dev4Amvj?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) in a letter to Maricopa County Recorder Justin Heap that he restore 24 voters the county attorney’s investigation found to be U.S. citizens from “Not Eligible” to active or inactive status. The letter stated the office is prepared to seek mandamus this week if he does not.**California** California voters will decide November 3 on Proposition 39, an initiative constitutional amendment that would [require](https://us.list-manage.com/c8DUWZv7IUU?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) government-issued identification to vote in person. The measure additionally would invalidate mail ballots lacking the last four digits of an ID number designated in the voter’s registration, and direct election officials to verify registrants’ citizenship with government data and report each county’s verification rate annually.The Riverside County Registrar of Voters [scheduled the destruction](https://us.list-manage.com/B4bTbMUJRnZ?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) of the roughly 650,000 November 2025 special election ballots returned by the sheriff, after the Secretary of State’s office advised that state law required it.Shasta County [left](https://us.list-manage.com/ByIZrRgd6ch?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the Redding city clerk race off November ballots. A county supervisor said the omission could require a special election costing $200,000 to $300,000.Twelve unvoted San Diego County mail ballots were [found](https://us.list-manage.com/ONr_IhGYO67?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) along a road outside Escondido. The Registrar of Voters said it found no sign of fraud or of loss in its custody and was working with the Postal Service to trace them.Humboldt County [mailed](https://us.list-manage.com/nYvmCAQdI85?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) voter information guides missing the statements of two local candidates. The county sent affected voters the statements with a letter explaining the error.Tulare County’s print vendor [mailed](https://us.list-manage.com/uKd3PjDXn5q?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) duplicate vote-by-mail ballots to 7,791 voters in the city of Tulare. The registrar said any second ballot returned will be rejected.Federal agents [arrested](https://us.list-manage.com/gAlLrNFbxuG?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) noncitizens for registering and voting in federal elections in a statewide operation that charged 28 lawful permanent residents across California’s four federal districts, including a Belizean national accused of voting in 2020, 2022, and 2024.An unknown number of mail ballots were [stolen](https://us.list-manage.com/7kPp3SbD5CQ?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) from a Daly City post office. San Mateo County election officials directed affected voters to request replacements while the Postal Inspection Service investigates.An Orange County prosecution of a Costa Mesa woman who registered her dog to vote and cast its ballot in the 2021 recall [ended in dismissal](https://us.list-manage.com/kW9T2qpGNXX?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) after she completed a plea agreement that required her to pay $1,500 for four anti-voter-fraud billboards.The Imperial County Registrar of Voters [mailed](https://us.list-manage.com/dTqwyvBgdcU?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) an extra ballot to about 160 confidential voters while changing its procedures for elected officials and candidates newly eligible for confidential status. Only one ballot per voter will be counted.**Colorado** About 835,000 voters in Adams, Arapahoe, Douglas, and Weld counties [received](https://us.list-manage.com/zFnvpysj7Yn?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) ballots carrying Issue 7A, a Front Range Passenger Rail District sales tax question, because the district did not tell county clerks the legislature had narrowed its boundaries. Counties will leave wholly ineligible precincts out of the 7A results and separate eligible ballots by hand in split precincts.Some Pueblo County residents, most in the Rye Fire District, [received](https://us.list-manage.com/1C2t91ZIwgP?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) a second ballot carrying only special district tax questions. The clerk’s office attributed the error to inaccurate voter lists supplied by the districts.**District of Columbia** The D.C. Board of Elections [asked](https://us.list-manage.com/5KCzgJ00ltn?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the National Guard to limit where its members are posted near drop boxes and voting sites after troops were seen beside a Foggy Bottom drop box. Joint Task Force-DC said its members are directed not to monitor or secure polling locations.**Florida** The Florida Department of Law Enforcement [arrested](https://us.list-manage.com/uSFn46VJfEV?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) a Palm Beach County man convicted of second-degree murder in 1998, whose voting rights were never restored, on two counts of false affirmation on voter registration applications and one count of voting as an unqualified elector.The Monroe County Supervisor of Elections [replaced](https://us.list-manage.com/uar3XJTSwMI?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the tabulators and electronic voter identification systems at the Big Pine Key early voting site after a resident found the building unlocked with the equipment unattended two days before early voting began. Officials said the equipment had not been tampered with.**Georgia** The Athens-Clarke County Elections Department [mailed](https://us.list-manage.com/7ASt3HY6BSO?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) a second absentee ballot to 1,154 voters after overlapping address lists went to its print vendor. The department said only one ballot per voter will be accepted.Poll workers [began handwriting](https://us.list-manage.com/166otJjO3Ri?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) each early voter’s name on a numbered list under a State Election Board rule that creates a paper record of who voted.**Illinois** Kendall County [sent](https://us.list-manage.com/8c2KkeTaszp?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) 300 mail ballots to two precincts carrying a referendum those voters were not eligible to decide, then spoiled and reissued them.**Indiana** Floyd County [left](https://us.list-manage.com/tt265TQD_0Y?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the District 1 county commissioner race off the early in-person and absentee ballots of 572 voters in four precincts because of a programming error. The county said affected voters will be able to cast corrected ballots.**Iowa** Warren County [sent](https://us.list-manage.com/IQr6OnQagvK?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) an extra absentee ballot to 613 voters, and Secretary of State Paul Pate said safeguards will ensure only one ballot from each is counted.**Kentucky** Caldwell County [printed](https://us.list-manage.com/ubGLsrk34NY?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the two candidates in a school board race in reverse of their drawn order. The clerk had vendor Harp Enterprises reprint the ballots after five absentee ballots had gone out.**Massachusetts** Some of the roughly 280 Pelham mail ballot packets [went out](https://us.list-manage.com/lvWuBfeO__d?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) with two copies of page one and no page two, which carries the last two referendum questions. The town clerk attributed the error to the vendor the Secretary of the Commonwealth hired to assemble the packets.The Cambridge Election Commission [warned](https://us.list-manage.com/znbcrVUemgs?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) that some of its pre-assembled mail ballot packets, also supplied by the Commonwealth, contained the same error.**Michigan** Tuscarora Township [mailed](https://us.list-manage.com/v48Qutao7W9?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) its absentee ballots more than a week after the statutory 40-day deadline. The deputy clerk apologized after the ACLU of Michigan threatened legal action.The Wayne County Board of Canvassers [counted](https://us.list-manage.com/UiVykRjsDTb?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) 37 absentee ballots excluded from Hamtramck’s 2025 mayoral count under a final court order, reversing the result. Certification is on hold pending a separate challenge to the winner’s residency.**Nevada** The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Nevada [announced](https://us.list-manage.com/OfYUZyi8hBS?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) an election integrity plan for early voting and Election Day.**New York** Monroe County’s mail ballot vendor [delayed](https://us.list-manage.com/11DC5GhtWZo?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) part of a batch of about 7,000 ballots because it lacked enough of the correct envelopes. County election commissioners said the remaining ballots have since been mailed.**North Carolina** Gov. Josh Stein [urged](https://us.list-manage.com/poYGcWcMxiu?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) voters to vote in person, citing an advocacy group’s analysis of 27 counties that found about 3% of mail ballots rejected so far, double the 2022 rate.**Oklahoma** The state’s online voter registration system [failed](https://us.list-manage.com/QZdM0RwF2Ia?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) for a couple of hours on the afternoon of the registration deadline because of a communication problem with Service Oklahoma’s data. The State Election Board did not extend the deadline.**Pennsylvania** Dauphin County [rejected](https://us.list-manage.com/B2CkADxFQoq?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) 10 mail ballot applications bearing repeated signatures and other irregularities. The district attorney’s investigation identified a person tied to a get-out-the-vote group who admitted falsifying them.Berks County’s mail ballots were [delayed](https://us.list-manage.com/M8RSiBzXKXF?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) by an envelope supply problem at the county’s printing vendor.**Tennessee** The DeKalb County Sheriff’s Department [charged](https://us.list-manage.com/o61yA5emqa1?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) Alexandria’s town recorder and court clerk with illegal registration or voting for allegedly denying a 2011 felony conviction on a June registration form and voting in the August election.**Texas** Counties [cleared](https://us.list-manage.com/15_kr1yF4xq?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the backlog of more than 500,000 voter registration records the Department of Public Safety had failed to transmit, according to the Secretary of State’s office. The office said affected registrants missing from the rolls may vote provisional ballots that will be counted.The Secretary of State’s office and its vendor Civix [re-sent](https://us.list-manage.com/122tvTGMH9I?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) counties about 15,000 online address updates submitted since September 1 that an extra address validation had held back. The office then sent some files again after counties found them missing the updated addresses.Nearly 1.8 million registrants, more than 9% of the state’s 19 million, [were on](https://us.list-manage.com/15Dz4jtdr5F?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the suspense list in figures the Secretary of State’s office released before early voting. Suspense voters who moved to another county may cast limited ballots only during early voting.**Utah** About 4,300 voters [received](https://us.list-manage.com/vege06fQ8lj?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) federal-only ballots because their citizenship could not yet be verified under HB 209’s documentary proof requirement for state and local races. They can obtain full ballots by verifying citizenship by October 23.**Virginia** Gov. Abigail Spanberger [said](https://us.list-manage.com/JEXgfXeGl7a?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) her administration is investigating why rights-restoration letters, which link recipients to voter registration, were sent to deceased Virginians.Attorney General Jay Jones [created](https://us.list-manage.com/Yiropxt0Kc9?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) a “Voter Protection Section” to investigate improper registration cancellations, absentee ballot denials, and voter intimidation and to enforce the Virginia Voting Rights Act.
---
|
---
| | **Oregon** Oregon Motor Voter ProgramComment deadline: November 10, 2026The Secretary of State [proposed amending OAR 165-005-0170](https://us.list-manage.com/s48AnY9zoPl?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a). The Secretary states the rule “replaces the previously adopted Oregon Motor Voter Registration Manual.” The “changes include notifications to qualified individuals during a covered transaction at DMV that their information is being sent to SoS for voter registration purposes, requiring OMV materials to be produced in multiple languages, updating contents of OMV notification mailed to registrants, updating the timing of [Oregon Motor Voter] data transfer from SoS to county election officials, updating processing instructions for county election officials, and requiring DMV and SoS to enter into an interagency agreement detailing file transfer specifications, daily control file policies, monthly audits, and SoS initiated list maintenance procedures.”
---
|
---
| | **Federal Agencies** _**Federal Communications Commission v. Brown**_**, No. 26-2230 (4th Cir.)** On October 14, the U.S. Supreme Court [stayed](https://us.list-manage.com/Zs9EOU4O6qM?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the Fourth Circuit’s October 7 mandamus order directing the Federal Communications Commission to rule within 48 hours on candidates’ challenge to its guidance that joint fundraising committees and coordinated political parties are entitled to broadcasters’ lowest unit charge. The Court reasoned that the Communications Act does not require the Commission to act on such applications within a particular timeframe.**Alabama** _**Alabama State Conference of the NAACP v. Attorney General of Alabama**_ , **No. 2:24-cv-00420 (N.D. Ala.)** On October 14, the Supreme Court of Alabama [heard argument](https://us.list-manage.com/SJ3Ggq5rf6Z?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) on questions certified by the Eleventh Circuit about the reach of SB 1’s payment and gift provisions on absentee-ballot application assistance. The questions include whether its exception for helping blind, disabled, or illiterate voters protects assistors.**California** _**United States v. California**_ , **No. 2:26-cv-12025 (C.D. Cal.)** On October 15, the U.S. Department of Justice [sued](https://us.list-manage.com/QwPZKo_3nXr?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) California, Secretary of State Shirley Weber, and Los Angeles County Registrar Dean Logan under the Supremacy Clause, seeking to bar the state from tabulating mail ballots cast by more than 20,000 registrants the federal government lists as likely noncitizens until their citizenship is verified. On October 19, the DOJ [applied](https://us.list-manage.com/1bk86B1H3Or?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) for a temporary restraining order requiring the state to set aside mail ballots from the more than 20,000 listed registrants until their citizenship is verified. The state and Los Angeles County [opposed the application](https://us.list-manage.com/KdWUtj9qDQP?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) on October 20._**Pico Neighborhood Association v. City of Santa Monica**_ , **No. BC616804 (Cal. Super. Ct., L.A. The parties have staked out widely divergent positions on specific reforms, but where does the American public stand when it comes to prioritizing one goal over the other?As part of my ongoing research on election administration and with recent support from the Grant Institute, I have collected survey data on public knowledge and opinions of state election procedures over several years. A total of twelve national surveys between 2008 and 2024 asked respondents whether the more important priority for their state should be “maximizing voter turnout even if some illegal voting occurs, or minimizing illegal voting even if that reduces turnout.”Over the entire period (N>11,000), Americans chose minimizing illegal voting over increasing turnout by a margin of more than two to one. Among those identifying most strongly with the Republican Party, the ratio exceeds ten to one, and among those who lean toward neither party the ratio is about 4.6 to one. In contrast, among strong Democrats the balance tips the other way, by about 1.5 to one in favor of increasing turnout. These ratios are also stable across years, although there is some evidence of increased polarization in 2024.These findings raise the question of whether the partisan divide reflects different views of the trade-offs or cues from party leaders. In a new study with David Doherty, Conor Dowling, and Michael Miller, I address this with two survey experiments conducted in 2024. Respondents chose between two voting rules for a hypothetical town. Under one, every eligible resident voted, but so did some ineligible residents; under the other, no ineligible residents voted, but fewer eligible residents did. We randomly varied the numbers on each side, as well as which party was said to have proposed each rule.Respondents in these experiments treated an illegal vote as far weightier than a lost legal one, giving roughly as much weight to one ineligible ballot as to ten eligible citizens not voting, and Democrats and Republicans responded to these trade-offs in much the same way, although Republicans were 18 to 19 percentage points more likely to favor eliminating illegal votes. Party cues, however, had enormous effects: support for the rule that eliminated illegal voting rose by 37 to 48 percentage points when it was attributed to the respondent’s own party.These findings suggest that much of the partisan conflict over voting rules reflects signals from party leaders rather than fundamentally different values. Americans across the political spectrum place a high priority on keeping ineligible votes out of elections, which leaves more room for compromise than the current debate would suggest.Professor Milyo’s article, coauthored with David Doherty, Conor M. | | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/9fecfe84a81b/stand-up-against-the-shameful-gop-power-grab-7363969?e=dc5f639d62)

Hey friends,I’m thrilled to share a special Memphis double drop with all of you! Memphis is having a moment, and I wanted you to hear it straight from two people who are living it.
[CLICK HERE to LISTEN NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/12qFCWZj6af?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)****
****[**Listen or watch**](https://us.list-manage.com/uYsrjzJqtAu?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)**now wherever you get your podcasts. 🎧**

First up is KeShaun Pearson, an organizer with Memphis Community Against Pollution and the brother of my good friend Rep. Justin J. Pearson. KeShaun lost both of his grandmothers to cancer in their early 60s, and he’ll tell you plainly why he believes environmental racism took them. That grief turned into knocking on doors in the rain with flyers printed at FedEx, and it’s still driving him today. We talk about Elon Musk’s xAI data centers, what happens to people’s trust when government sides with corporations over community, and who in the world responds to violent policy with civility.Then I sit down with Jerri Green, Memphis City Councilwoman and the Democratic nominee for governor. Jerri doesn’t take money from special interests, but she’ll tell you she has three: Bo, Vivian, and Wilder. We talk about what she hears from Tennesseans from Memphis to the mountains, her plans for day one, putting money back in your pocket instead of handing out corporate tax breaks, and a couple of stories about Marsha Blackburn that you’re going to have to hear to believe.Two different roles, one message: Memphis ain’t nothing to play with, and neither is Tennessee. Early voting runs through October 29th, and Election Day is Tuesday, November 3rd. Make your plan to vote, bring somebody with you, and vote the whole ballot.
Thank you for being here,
Gloria

Each month features beautiful photography celebrating God's creation, encouraging passages of Scripture, and space to record your prayer requests and blessings. As the year unfolds, your calendar can become a meaningful reminder of the prayers you've offered and the many ways God has been faithful. **And when you request your calendar today, you can help answer a very real need for a mother facing an unexpected pregnancy.** Every day, women across America are searching for hope in the midst of fear and uncertainty. Through PreBorn!'s Network Clinics, these mothers can receive free ultrasounds, compassionate care, and the opportunity to hear about the new life found in Jesus Christ. **Your gift of just $28 helps provide one life-saving ultrasound** , giving a mother the opportunity to see her baby, hear the heartbeat, and recognize the precious life growing within her. As our thank-you for your gift of any amount, we'll send you our beautiful 2027 calendar, which also includes a **special Ministry Prayer Guide** to help you lift up mothers, babies, families, and the lifesaving work of PreBorn! throughout the year.

| Peter,
Our grandparents marched so that Black Louisianans could have a voice in Congress. They bled for it. Some died for it.
Then the Supreme Court gutted the Voting Rights Act. Gov. Landry declared a "state of emergency" and canceled an election already underway, so he could erase one of our majority Black districts.
In places like Scotlandville, LA the people are losing Democrat Cleo Fields, the man who grew up on their streets and carried their voice to Washington.

| | | Oregon didn't just adopt vote-by-mail. We INVENTED it. **So when President Trump signs an executive order restricting mail-in ballots, understand what that means: ** No state has more on the line than Oregon. This order isn't aimed at some abstract "voting system." **It targets how every single Oregonian votes.** Here's what Trump’s USPS order does. It orders the Postal Service to deliver ballots only to voters on a federal list — a list built by THIS administration. Their postmaster already said the quiet part out loud: states that don't hand over their voter data likely won't have mail ballots delivered at all. Now here's what I know. **I'm Oregon's chief elections officer. We have taken this administration to court — over their demand for your voter data, and over their first election order. We won.** _**They still are not stopping. **_ **The Constitution hasn't changed**. States run elections. Not presidents. Not postmasters. And this November, Oregon will run the same safe, fair, accurate vote-by-mail election we've run for 25 years — and I will use every power of this office to make sure of it. **[But fighting them in court is only one way to defend our elections. We must have the resources to communicate about what’s at stake — every lawsuit, every rule change, every attempt to rewrite how Oregon votes. That’s why I’m using my campaign to help travel around the state and talk directly to voters too. Chip in to help us keep fighting.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141929745/655238226/-569431239?refcode=261022-invented-rs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkNDUwOWQ2Ni0xOWNlLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=4c57c-RwlcZ8aQo0Pmj3PA3loNm-N8teN3t0AbWX2z8=)**

clean_body: | | | = | | | Oregon didn't just adopt vote-by-mail. We INVENTED it. So when President Trump signs an executive order restricting mail-in ballots, understand what that means: No state has more on the line than Oregon. This order isn't aimed at some abstract "voting system." It targets how every single Oregonian votes. Here's what Trump’s USPS order does. It orders the Postal Service to deliver ballots only to voters on a federal list — a list built by THIS administration. Their postmaster already said the quiet part out loud: states that don't hand over their voter data likely won't have mail ballots delivered at all. Now here's what I know. I'm Oregon's chief elections officer. We have taken this administration to court — over their demand for your voter data, and over their first election order. We won. They still are not stopping. The Constitution hasn't changed. States run elections. Not presidents. Not postmasters. And this November, Oregon will run the same safe, fair, accurate vote-by-mail election we've run for 25 years — and I will use every power of this office to make sure of it. = = They think they can push around a small state like Oregon. This evil administration is dead set on dismantling every critical program serving working people in need - programs that were a _lifeline_ for my family when I was growing up.
I know firsthand the crushing anxiety that comes with not knowing where your next meal will come from. It is unacceptable that any human being goes hungry in the richest country on earth.
**Sadly, my opponent Andy Barr and his idol Mitch McConnell voted for this.** They _proudly_ voted in favor of Trump's Big Beautiful Bill.
These cuts have already affected 24,655 children and 6,572 seniors in Kentucky - America's most vulnerable are being kicked aside while the wealthiest get tax cuts. It's not only illogical, but it's also despicable.
We can't afford to keep going on like this. I won't settle for one more child going hungry by way of this cruel administration.

When a local prosecutor weighs immigration status in deciding charges and plea deals, two people who commit the same crime in the same community can face very different consequences. A House investigation and a Department of Justice civil rights probe now allege that's not a hypothetical -- it's policy, in writing, in jurisdictions from Northern Virginia to Colorado to Philadelphia.
Start in Fairfax County, Virginia. Commonwealth's Attorney Steve Descano's office adopted guidelines in December 2020 -- his first year in office -- instructing assistant prosecutors to consider immigration consequences where possible and where doing so accords with justice in plea bargaining, charging decisions, and sentencing. On May 6, 2026, the Justice Department's Civil Rights Division notified Descano it was opening an investigation to determine whether his office discriminated against United States citizens by offering preferential treatment only to illegal alien criminal defendants. Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon put it bluntly: the Division "will not allow local prosecutors to pick and choose winners based on their immigration status," and the probe would examine "sweetheart deals to illegal immigrants charged with serious crimes."
Eight days later, Descano was on Capitol Hill testifying before the House Judiciary Committee's hearing, "Fairfax County, Virginia: The Dangerous Consequences of Sanctuary Policies." His answer to all of it: the policies are fair and legal, and the investigations are "political nonsense."...

Hi Peter — it’s Alexander Vindman. I am reaching out today with a personal request.
[**Can you contribute $5, $20, $50, or any amount to my twin brother Eugene’s campaign for Congress today? We’re just weeks out from Election Day and Eugene needs your help to win his race against his MAGA opponent.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/evfc-em-oct26?refcode=em261022-av&refcode2=1166_3892029_EPMwh9&akid=1166%2E3892029%2EEPMwh9)

Many of you know our story by now, but I want to take a moment to remind you why Eugene is in this fight.
Over two decades ago, Eugene and I swore an oath to protect our country, its people, and our democracy from harm's way when we joined the U.S. Army. Our oath was tested in 2019 when Eugene and I decided to uphold our patriotic duty and blow the whistle on Donald Trump’s corruption.
We reported Trump’s phone call with Ukraine, and our actions eventually led to his first impeachment. That decision to stand up for the integrity of the office of the presidency led to us both being fired by Trump — ending our decades-long careers in military service.
But Eugene wouldn't let Trump’s vengeance stop his service to our country. Over 7 years after that phone call, Eugene is serving the people of Virginia’s 7th district in Congress. And now, he’s up for re-election for the first time against a MAGA extremist.
Eugene has seen the danger Donald Trump and MAGA extremism pose to our democracy firsthand in Congress. And he understands that our best path to stopping Trump is to put a check on his power by flipping the House blue.
But here’s the truth: Democrats cannot take back the House unless Eugene holds his seat. If he loses, we have virtually no path to the House majority and no path to stopping Trump’s corruption.
So with just 18 days remaining until the Election, he needs our unwavering support to take on his extremist opponent and WIN.
So I am sincerely asking:
[**Can you chip in $5, $10, or whatever you can afford today to help Eugene win his race? |

| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141940247/655264389/-977686964?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_ReintroductionRS_261022_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZTI1MjBkZi0xZWNlLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ysqIox5y7mhb7xfenvfdweu0jZQA05_ZObK8SgY4JPM=) Derek,

I know I’ve been sending you a lot of emails about my reelection race in Virginia these days, and today, I want to take a step back and reintroduce myself.

[_**But first, with just 12 days until Election Day, I'm hoping you'll consider chipping in to my reelection campaign to protect this must-win Senate seat for Democrats and take back control of Congress.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141940248/655264391/-977686964?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_ReintroductionRS_261022_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZTI1MjBkZi0xZWNlLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ysqIox5y7mhb7xfenvfdweu0jZQA05_ZObK8SgY4JPM=)

Like so many Americans, I grew up in a middle-class family and was lucky enough to attend good public schools. I have my 8th grade history teacher to thank for setting me on the path to being a Democrat. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141940250/655264392/-977686964?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_ReintroductionRS_261022_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZTI1MjBkZi0xZWNlLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ysqIox5y7mhb7xfenvfdweu0jZQA05_ZObK8SgY4JPM=) Fast forward a few years, I became the first person in my family to graduate from college, made possible by working multiple jobs and taking out student loans.

Before I became a U.S. Senator, I actually started out in business. I invested my entire life savings, a few thousand dollars, into my first venture... which failed in about six weeks, by the way. My second venture did a little better, lasting six months, but it wasn’t until my third try that things started to look up. I’m extremely proud to have founded what became one of Virginia’s leading tech companies.

It was actually that experience that got me into public service. I thought that everybody in this country ought to have the same kind of fair shot that I had. So, I ran for governor in Virginia, and won. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141940251/655264393/-977686964?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_ReintroductionRS_261022_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZTI1MjBkZi0xZWNlLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ysqIox5y7mhb7xfenvfdweu0jZQA05_ZObK8SgY4JPM=) And if you can believe it, my good friend Tim Kaine (now my fellow Virginia senator) was my Lieutenant Governor. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141940252/655264394/-977686964?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_ReintroductionRS_261022_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZTI1MjBkZi0xZWNlLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ysqIox5y7mhb7xfenvfdweu0jZQA05_ZObK8SgY4JPM=) After our four years in the governor’s office, Virginia was rated the best state for business, the best managed state, _and_ the best state to receive an education. But even then, I knew that my work to make sure that _every_ family – no matter their background – has the same shot that I did, was far from over.

That’s when I ran for the United States Senate, and won. That year, President Obama won in Virginia too – the first time the Commonwealth of Virginia voted for a Democratic presidential nominee since 1964. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141940253/655264396/-977686964?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_ReintroductionRS_261022_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZTI1MjBkZi0xZWNlLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ysqIox5y7mhb7xfenvfdweu0jZQA05_ZObK8SgY4JPM=) In the Senate, I helped spearhead the largest infrastructure and public lands investments in half a century, worked to significantly expand Virginia’s domestic manufacturing, and have fought to lower health care costs across the Commonwealth. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141940254/655264397/-977686964?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_ReintroductionRS_261022_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZTI1MjBkZi0xZWNlLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ysqIox5y7mhb7xfenvfdweu0jZQA05_ZObK8SgY4JPM=) **But I have to tell you, in my time in the Senate – maybe in my time in politics – there has been nothing as challenging, as bizarre, and as _holy sugar_ as the second Trump administration.**

This administration's incompetence has made every American less safe. The president’s tariffs and reckless foreign policy have caused prices to skyrocket for working families. His administration is peddling conspiracy theories about our elections and undermining American’s faith in our democracy. And my Republican colleagues continue to fail at holding him accountable.

I didn’t get into politics to let people like Trump dismantle our federal government and rebuild it for himself and his allies. I’m proud to lead the fight against this corrupt administration, but I can’t do it alone.

[_**I’m asking Virginians to re-hire me one last time so I can keep up my work holding this administration accountable and delivering for Virginia. Can I count on you to pitch in to my campaign so we can win BIG on Election Day?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141940256/655264398/-977686964?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_ReintroductionRS_261022_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZTI1MjBkZi0xZWNlLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ysqIox5y7mhb7xfenvfdweu0jZQA05_ZObK8SgY4JPM=)

The fight continues,

Mark Warner ********[Contribute](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141940257/655264399/-977686964?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_ReintroductionRS_261022_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZTI1MjBkZi0xZWNlLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ysqIox5y7mhb7xfenvfdweu0jZQA05_ZObK8SgY4JPM=)********

body:
The amount of threats I am receiving is just off the charts.
# [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=2545%2E791427%2EcCL_09)
[](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-dhs-oct26.4A7Axt&refcode=em261022-1-180&t=2&akid=2545%2E791427%2EcCL_09)
It’s true.
I have to move out of the home that Trump sent his DHS goons to raid just last week. And I’ll tell you why.
For years now, I have received a daily barrage of racist attacks, death threats, stalkers, and people who threaten the folks around me. These threats spike every time Trump speaks my name, and they eventually resulted in a man coming to a town hall meeting in Minneapolis in January and attacking me.
But now that Trump has brought the full force of his fascist administration down on me, the amount of threats I am receiving is just **_off the charts._**
As you know, this entire investigation is a big nothing that will go nowhere. The only thing this raid actually accomplished is that MAGA and the media have now broadcast my family’s DC address to the same crazy people who threaten my life. **My own home is no longer safe, and so I have to move.**
Friend, this is exactly why I take my security seriously. If my security team wasn’t there to apprehend my attacker at that town hall, who knows what could have happened.
The problem is that paying for a security team is expensive. Congress does not provide one to me. I have to pay for my own safety from my campaign’s pockets.
So, I’m reaching out today to humbly ask for your help in continuing to ensure the security of me, my family, and my entire campaign team as we keep up the fight against the corrupt criminals in the White House.

**GREENWICH, CT** -- Jonathan Goldstein, Republican candidate for Connecticut's 150th House District, is calling for answers after federal earnings data showed Connecticut's female-to-male median weekly earnings ratio falling from 97% in 2020 to 79.6% in 2025.
[Pledge your support](https://substack..1Mzdb4i7hzyJb-mv_Aobi40eH5pPpGBw6Mks5TUR9xw?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=221634630)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1ea202d9-ab86-4ec7-a476-8b06ba0bd64e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[View Campaign Site](https://substack.com/redirect/40dcd567-33c8-4784-82d1-e88bcbbca06d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Source USA Facts using Bureau of Labor Statistics Data](https://substack.com/redirect/ed80a465-e769-46c0-b1d1-d0035b2a0180?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
"Six years ago, Connecticut women were earning approximately 97 cents for every dollar earned by men. Today, that figure is below 80 cents," Goldstein said. "What happened to equal opportunity, and why isn't Hartford demanding answers?"
According to Bureau of Labor Statistics data compiled by [USAFacts](https://substack.com/redirect/ed80a465-e769-46c0-b1d1-d0035b2a0180?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Connecticut's reported ratio declined by 17.4 percentage points. The figures do not establish the causes of the decline.
Goldstein contrasted Connecticut's performance with neighboring New York, where women working full-time, year-round earned 91.4 cents for every dollar earned by men in 2024, according to New York State Department of Labor data. Although the two figures use different statistical measures, Goldstein said the comparison raises important questions about economic opportunity.
**" This is bigger than national politics. New York doesn't appear to have the same problem to this extent. Connecticut has its own legislature, its own economy and its own responsibilities. Hartford needs to be held accountable."**
### **Economic Independence Is Also a Women 's Safety Issue**
Speaking during Domestic Violence Awareness Month, Goldstein connected the wage gap to women's financial independence and personal safety, an issue he raised at the League of Women Voters candidate forum.
"When women earn less, it becomes harder to afford housing, raise families, save for retirement or leave an abusive relationship. Economic independence is not just about opportunity. Sometimes it is about survival."
Greenwich's October 2026 Domestic Violence Awareness proclamation identifies domestic violence as the town's most-reported violent crime and reports more than 3,600 hotline calls to YWCA Greenwich Domestic Abuse Services during the preceding year.
"These are our mothers, daughters, sisters and neighbors. We need to ensure that women have both the economic opportunities and the public safety protections they deserve."
### **Affordability, Opportunity and Local Control**
Goldstein, _**who has received the endorsement of the Fraternal Order of Police**_ , said effective policing, victim protection and cooperation with local domestic violence organizations must remain priorities.
"Greenwich police officers and local service providers understand our community. Hartford should be supporting their ability to protect victims, not making their jobs harder."
Goldstein said the issue reflects his campaign's **ABCs: Affordability, Beaches and Local Control.**
"Affordability isn't just about what you pay. It's about what you earn, what you can save and whether you can afford to live independently."
Goldstein concluded:
**" Connecticut women deserve better than a widening wage gap and political excuses. Hartford needs to explain what happened, examine the causes and work toward real solutions.**
**" We need a Connecticut where women can earn a fair living, raise their families, build financial security and live safely. That's what equal opportunity should mean."**

#### **[Susan Collins Applauds Release of 315,000 Barrels from Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve](https://substack.com/redirect/36c102ee-30ab-49eb-bf2e-6de169a66e4f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
The Trump administration will release up to 315,000 barrels from the Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve, a month after Sens. Susan Collins and Angus King asked for it. That's equal to a 13% supply increase for New England, and 200,000 of the reserve's barrels sit in South Portland. As some forecasters are privately warning that home heating oil could reach $8.00 per gallon this winter, the hope is that surplus supply will bid down the cost. In 26 years, the reserve has been tapped only twice, in 2011 to swap in cleaner oil and in 2012 after Hurricane Sandy. This is the first time it's been used to bring prices down. [Seamus Othot has the story](https://substack.com/redirect/36c102ee-30ab-49eb-bf2e-6de169a66e4f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

#### **[Waterville Police Arrest Suspect After He Threatened to Murder Officers During Six-Hour Standoff](https://substack.com/redirect/6c827b9c-0bc5-46cb-9893-8a0a4e201f9a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Waterville police went to 10 Autumn St. around 6 p.m. Tuesday with a terrorizing warrant for John Whitney, 41, over threats he allegedly made online. Police say he wouldn't open the door, threatened to shoot officers, and after several hours of negotiating started throwing knives at them. The State Police tactical team came in around 11 p.m., and an hour later Whitney was in custody. Police say he faces five charges, including aggravated reckless conduct and criminal threatening with a dangerous weapon. Corrections records show a John Whitney of the same age on probation in Waterville, sentenced in 2025 to three years for assaulting a police officer and let out early on probation. Those conditions barred him from having dangerous weapons. It isn't confirmed he's the same man.

#### **[Oft-Arrested Litchfield Man Busted Again After Fleeing Police With Incorrect Plates](https://substack.com/redirect/ee68fe4e-b36b-4371-8efb-dae1144f809b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
A Kennebec deputy in Augusta ran the plates on a Subaru Outback Monday night and they came back to a BMW X5. Deputies say the driver went the wrong way down a one-way street, then led them toward Belgrade at more than 80 mph before bailing out on foot on West Road. The deputy recognized him: Joshua Tilley, 43, of Litchfield, whom he had arrested several times before. Deputies say Tilley faces seven charges, including violating conditions of release, driving to endanger and attaching false plates, and is held without bail. He was arrested in 2019 after he allegedly kidnapped his girlfriend and fled police.
#### **[Lisbon Drunk Driver Crashes Into Building Then Utility Pole Before Being Arrested](https://substack.com/redirect/610256b8-60f2-48de-8b4c-6cb749a52a4f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Lisbon police say a car left Route 196 around 6:22 p.m. Sunday, hit a building near School Street, kept going and took out a utility pole near Aubuchon Hardware, dropping power lines. Lisbon Street stayed closed until 11:22 p.m. Police say Joseph St. Amant, 70, of Lisbon, was charged with OUI. The next night, another car on Route 196 hit a two-unit apartment building on School Street. That driver went to the hospital, police haven't named him or her, and charges are expected.

#### **[Portland School Official's Dog Proposal: Puppies Behind Plexiglass?](https://substack.com/redirect/86d2d5ee-62d1-49ae-b82d-d7d155d8563f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
A follow-up to Tuesday's item. At the Oct. 14 Portland Public Schools policy committee meeting, assistant superintendent Abdullahi Ahmed asked that students opt in to dog activities, such as therapy-animal events, rather than parents having to opt them out, citing Islamic teaching that "dog saliva is considered impure." The meeting ran an hour. The board's most creative idea came from member Maya Lena, who floated keeping the puppies in a plexiglass enclosure so students "could interact with the puppies without touching the dogs or getting their fluids on them."

## Maine Wire TV
**If you 're reading this, you probably get Maine Wire TV delivered via Substack. But you can also watch us on Facebook, X, and YouTube. You can subscribe on Apple or Spotify, too! Here's yesterday's episode...**
[](https://substack.com/redirect/dd611a99-0f6b-4f87-8413-c557ba0588d4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**[Jon Fetherston's Lewiston City Hall Confrontation](https://substack.com/redirect/d6e84895-d2fc-4cd3-ada1-1a540d62c190?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**: Tom Shattuck hosts Jon Fetherston, Seamus Othot, Graham and me. Jon describes a voter at Lewiston City Hall who told him to meet him in the street, his exchange with Safiya Khalid, and the translators helping voters, many of whom he says registered the same day. I walk through how Chinese-run illegal marijuana grows use the hemp loophole to sell out of state.
## Today's Political Events

Oct 22 | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- The Trump administration will release up to 315,000 barrels from the Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve, a month after Sens. Susan Collins and Angus King asked for it. That's equal to a 13% supply increase for New England, and 200,000 of the reserve's barrels sit in South Portland. As some forecasters are privately warning that home heating oil could reach $8.00 per gallon this winter, the hope is that surplus supply will bid down the cost. In 26 years, the reserve has been tapped only twice, in 2011 to swap in cleaner oil and in 2012 after Hurricane Sandy. This is the first time it's been used to bring prices down. . Like this kind of reporting? Subscribe to The Robinson Report for the latest news moving Maine politics. Subscribe free at RobinsonReport.Substack.com Waterville police went to 10 Autumn St. around 6 p.m. Tuesday with a terrorizing warrant for John Whitney, 41, over threats he allegedly made online. Police say he wouldn't open the door, threatened to shoot officers, and after several hours of negotiating started throwing knives at them. The State Police tactical team came in around 11 p.m., and an hour later Whitney was in custody. Police say he faces five charges, including aggravated reckless conduct and criminal threatening with a dangerous weapon. Corrections records show a John Whitney of the same age on probation in Waterville, sentenced in 2025 to three years for assaulting a police officer and let out early on probation. Those conditions barred him from having dangerous weapons. It isn't confirmed he's the same man. | | ---|---|--- A Kennebec deputy in Augusta ran the plates on a Subaru Outback Monday night and they came back to a BMW X5. Deputies say the driver went the wrong way down a one-way street, then led them toward Belgrade at more than 80 mph before bailing out on foot on West Road. The deputy recognized him: Joshua Tilley, 43, of Litchfield, whom he had arrested several times before. Deputies say Tilley faces seven charges, including violating conditions of release, driving to endanger and attaching false plates, and is held without bail. He was arrested in 2019 after he allegedly kidnapped his girlfriend and fled police. Lisbon police say a car left Route 196 around 6:22 p.m. Sunday, hit a building near School Street, kept going and took out a utility pole near Aubuchon Hardware, dropping power lines. Lisbon Street stayed closed until 11:22 p.m. Police say Joseph St. Amant, 70, of Lisbon, was charged with OUI. The next night, another car on Route 196 hit a two-unit apartment building on School Street. That driver went to the hospital, police haven't named him or her, and charges are expected. | | ---|---|--- A follow-up to Tuesday's item. At the Oct. 14 Portland Public Schools policy committee meeting, assistant superintendent Abdullahi Ahmed asked that students opt in to dog activities, such as therapy-animal events, rather than parents having to opt them out, citing Islamic teaching that "dog saliva is considered impure." The meeting ran an hour. The board's most creative idea came from member Maya Lena, who floated keeping the puppies in a plexiglass enclosure so students "could interact with the puppies without touching the dogs or getting their fluids on them." A federal judge just ruled against the Department of Homeland Security's attempts to conduct unjustified stops and door to door sweeps as part of Trump's bogus "Unlawful Voter Initiative."
The "Surge" as they referred to it internally at DHS relied on "error-prone government lists" that were shown to be sweeping U.S. citizens into the DHS dragnet -- putting at risk thousands of valid voters in the Trump Admin's quixotic quest to find voter fraud committed by non-citizens.
Now it isn't just ICE conducting raids and questioning anyone who looks "foreign": DHS' "Homeland Security Investigations" is taking the lead, the very same branch of the agency that conducted the raid on Rep. Ilhan Omar.

Sen. Mark Kelly (D-Arizona) called this out as voter intimidation and urged citizens to not be deterred, to make sure their votes are cast and counted.
We agree. But our work is more crucial now than ever: and Defend Our Courts' Emergency GOTV funds are already being used to help any voters who sent mail-in ballots disenfranchised in North Carolina--way ahead of schedule and completely unexpected this early in the voting.

Are we seeking freedom--or grieving the foundations that make it meaningful?
The kitchen table is our first crucible. There, we learn the weight of our voices and the gravity of responsibility. We discover that love is not a transaction, and our choices ripple toward those bound to us.
Erich Fromm explored how freedom can bring isolation, tempting us to trade our judgment for the certainty of belonging. We often mistake the constraints of connection for the chains of oppression. Yet, in escaping obligation, we risk weakening the very foundations that help us stand.
Family is where love, duty, and conflict meet. Traditions can burden us, but viewing family solely as an obstacle to independence is a dangerous trade. A healthy family gives us roots and the courage to meet the world without losing ourselves.
Freedom is the capacity to choose, to care, and to remain accountable.
**Pause. Breathe. Look Deeper.**
**Refuel.**
**Welcome to Sweet Ground.**

The kitchen table is our first crucible. There, we learn the weight of our voices and the gravity of responsibility. We discover that love is not a transaction, and our choices ripple toward those bound to us. Erich Fromm explored how freedom can bring isolation, tempting us to trade our judgment for the certainty of belonging. We often mistake the constraints of connection for the chains of oppression. Yet, in escaping obligation, we risk weakening the very foundations that help us stand. Family is where love, duty, and conflict meet. Traditions can burden us, but viewing family solely as an obstacle to independence is a dangerous trade. A healthy family gives us roots and the courage to meet the world without losing ourselves. # This is it, Friend
---
| | | | | | Friend,
This is it. In just a few days, this campaign comes down to the wire, and October 27 is our final fundraising deadline before New Mexicans finish casting their ballots.I'll be straight with you about what that deadline means. Every dollar we raise before October 27 decides how long we stay on the air in the final stretch. Television, digital, mail: those are the voters we reach, or the voters we don't.
My opponent has deep pockets and national money behind her. We have something better: thousands of New Mexicans who believe this state can be safer, more affordable, and run by someone who has actually delivered results. I spent twelve years as Mayor of Rio Rancho proving that. I showed up to answer the tough questions at the KOB debate when my opponent didn't. And I am going to keep showing up all the way to Election Day.
But I can't do it without you.
Whatever you can spare today, whether that's $25, $50, $100, or more, goes straight to keeping our message in front of voters through the final days of this race. If you've already given, thank you. If you can give one more time before the deadline, now is when it matters most.

name: Roy Cooper
subject: Two dollars today
body:
We have a situation, Peter.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1717&source=&t=1&akid=4785%2E124072%2El5UZp8) | | | |
---
Peter,
Here’s the situation: We’re still coming up short of our $500,000 midnight fundraising goal. This is a goal we _have_ to hit to get our final ads on the air and keep up our momentum in the final weeks of this race.
**That’s why I’m switching things up. I’m lowering my fundraising ask to just $2 today. That’s right – just $2.**
[**_Will you chip in $2 right now to help us reach our critical goal before 11:59 p.m., flip North Carolina blue and take back the Senate for Democrats?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1717&t=8&akid=4785%2E124072%2El5UZp8)
I know that $2 might feel small – but it’s not just your $2. When thousands of grassroots supporters chip in $2 or whatever they can, it adds up fast and builds the momentum we need to win.
$2 because North Carolina is the best chance for Democrats to flip a Republican-held Senate seat in the country.
$2 because if we lose here, we’ll lose our shot at taking back the majority.
$2 because GOP dark-money super PACs have invested millions into false attack ads against me.
$2 because we can make life better for working people, put an end to the chaos and stop President Trump’s cruel agenda – but only if we come together.
**I’m counting on you, Peter. We’re running out of time to fund our final ads of this campaign.[_Will you please chip in $2 to help us reach our fundraising goal so we can flip NC and the Senate?_](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1717&t=9&akid=4785%2E124072%2El5UZp8)**
_If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_ | | | [DONATE $2](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15913?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1717&t=10&akid=4785%2E124072%2El5UZp8)

Thank you,

Roy Cooper
| |
* * *
[](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1717&t=2&akid=4785%2E124072%2El5UZp8)
Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

[**_Donate today to help win this seat and flip the Senate blue._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1717&source=&t=3&akid=4785%2E124072%2El5UZp8)

body:
[ stdin# ]Josh Shapiro for Pennsylvania
Derek,

Since we kicked off this reelection campaign
nearly ten months ago, I’ve heard from so many Pennsylvanians from all
across our Commonwealth. I’ve heard your stories, your concerns, and your
kind words.

But I’ve also heard a lot of questions — so I wanted to use this email to
address some FAQs about this final stretch of the election. (But listen,
if you’re already up-to-date on everything going on here in Pennsylvania,
[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/19746?t=1001&akid=703%2E245147%2EPRl9T5 ]please use this link to rush a donation before midnight. Every dollar
counts!)

Question 1: What is the state of the race right now?

It’s... complex, to say the least. If you only paid attention to the polls
and the pundits, they’d tell you we’re in the lead right now. And sure,
Derek, I think
we’re in the lead too. But here in Pennsylvania — the most competitive
battleground state in the country — leads have a tendency to evaporate. At
the very last second.

So throughout these final twelve days, we’re going to run this race
full-speed ahead: TV ads, on-the-ground organizers, rallies, events. All
of it makes a difference, and all of it takes resources.

Question 2: What makes this election different?

Look, I believe any election in Pennsylvania is important. But this
Governor’s race in 2026? It’s not only about Pennsylvania’s future. It’s
about our entire country’s future. Our entire democracy’s future.

If my opponent wins on November 3rd, Republicans will control every
state-level office in Pennsylvania. So come 2028, when Donald Trump almost
certainly tries to cast doubt on our elections and lean on his enablers to
undermine them? We need a Governor who will stand up to him — not someone
who will help him overturn an election.

Question 3: How can I help?

The best way to make an impact at this point in the election is to [ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/19746?t=1002&akid=703%2E245147%2EPRl9T5 ]make
a donation of any amount to our campaign — seriously, even just one dollar
makes a difference! Trust me, I wish it didn’t take so much money to win
an election either. But my opponent has the full backing of Donald Trump
and his network of Mar-a-Lago donors. And the only way we can fight back
against that kind of cash is with an overwhelming, effective response.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/19746?t=1003&akid=703%2E245147%2EPRl9T5 ]So Derek, if
any of those answers convinced you, will you chip in as much as you can to
make these final twelve days count? In a state like Pennsylvania, your
donation could literally be the difference between winning and losing.

If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your
donation will go through immediately:

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/19747?t=1004&akid=703%2E245147%2EPRl9T5 ]Donate $5 →

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/19748?t=1005&akid=703%2E245147%2EPRl9T5 ]Donate $15 →

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/19749?t=1006&akid=703%2E245147%2EPRl9T5 ]Donate $25 →

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/19750?t=1007&akid=703%2E245147%2EPRl9T5 ]Donate $50 →

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/19751?t=1008&akid=703%2E245147%2EPRl9T5 ]Donate $100 →

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/19746?t=1009&akid=703%2E245147%2EPRl9T5 ]Other →

Thank you,

Josh Shapiro

People who want assurance.

Peter, After serving our country for 35 years in the Navy, I was removed from my position by Pete Hegseth without reason. I spent my entire life in service to this country, always putting the mission and the people above myself. But when I was forced out, I had a choice: go out quietly, or _find a way to keep serving._ Peter, I’ve always lived by three simple ideals: honor, integrity, and respect. **That’s why I’m running for Congress in South Carolina’s first district.**[If you believe that’s what we need in Washington right now, please consider splitting $10 between my campaign and the Democratic Party of Georgia.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141949536/655288147/-1148897003?amount=10&source=DPG_EM_FR_102226_B1_LacoreSplit_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTA4MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3YTAzZTM0MC0yN2NlLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=qWqECq9EB7aKUCoJdXual31WDYfrzzNTxQL8OTR3j-Q=) | | [DONATE $10 >>](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141949537/655288148/-1148897003?amount=10&source=DPG_EM_FR_102226_B1_LacoreSplit_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTA4MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3YTAzZTM0MC0yN2NlLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=qWqECq9EB7aKUCoJdXual31WDYfrzzNTxQL8OTR3j-Q=)

The day I was removed from my position, I was forced to leave behind my life’s work. I never went back to the Pentagon or wore the uniform again.
But this story isn’t just about me. Throughout the first year of Donald Trump’s second term, every woman serving as a three or four-star admiral in the Navy has been fired, forced out, or reassigned. This wasn’t an isolated incident, Peter. It’s a pattern.
When leadership decisions are driven by politics instead of integrity, our families, communities, and nation pay the price.
**That’s why I’m running for Congress:** to keep serving, to stand up when it’s hardest, and to fight for leadership that puts country over politics every time.

Some doors have been closed for 237 years

| | Peter, The United States Senate has existed since 1789. In those 237 years, no Native American woman has ever served in it. The governor's office of any state? Same story. **Both of those doors could open on the same night on November 3rd.** **Peggy Flanagan** , a citizen of the White Earth Nation, is 1.8 points ahead in a race RealClearPolitics calls a toss-up — one hold away from that Senate first. **Deb Haaland** , a citizen of Laguna Pueblo, leads her governor's race in New Mexico — _a state that didn't let Native Americans vote until 1948_. From barred-from-the-ballot to the governor's desk, in one long lifetime. And **Mary Peltola** , a Yup'ik leader who already made history as the first Alaska Native in Congress, is in the dead heat Senate race that could decide the majority itself. We’re going to break that historic barrier on Election Night. But the work required to do so must be done right now. _You're getting this message because you’ve supported good causes and Democratic candidates. We need your support to continue fighting for our democracy. We love having you in our network, but if you only want our most important email updates,[click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/108?t=2&akid=3619%2E259176%2ECe4cbt) If you'd like to unsubscribe, [click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/109?t=3&akid=3619%2E259176%2ECe4cbt)_

[]( https://act.blueampaction.com/go/17838?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.10.22_Nixon-Corporations_B3_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON&t=4&akid=3619%2E259176%2ECe4cbt) Peter, it's Angie Nixon, Democratic Nominee for U.S. Senate.

Here's a con that's been running for years, and it's time someone said it out loud.

Politicians like Ashley Moody keep getting richer in office. Meanwhile, the rest of us are working harder than ever and still can't get ahead.

And when people ask why, here's the answer they get: you should have worked harder.

Not the corporation that underpays you. Not the executives who padded their own bonuses while freezing your wages. Not the politicians who wrote the laws that let them do it.

You.

That's the con. Blame the nurse, the warehouse worker, the teacher, the home health aide, for a system that was rigged against them before they ever walked in the door.

I've watched this happen my whole life. My mom worked two jobs just to keep us afloat, not because she didn't work hard enough, but because the system was never built for people like us to get ahead in the first place.

That's why I'm running for U.S. Senate. To fix a broken system that punishes work and rewards exploitation.

Because the problem was never hard work. The problem is a government that lets corporations underpay people, then hands politicians like Moody a growing net worth for looking the other way. [**CCan you split $5, $10, or whatever you can between Blue Amp Action and me today to help us end this con before Election Day?**]( https://act.blueampaction.com/go/17838?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.10.22_Nixon-Corporations_B3_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON&t=5&akid=3619%2E259176%2ECe4cbt) | [CHIP IN $10]( https://act.blueampaction.com/go/17838?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.10.22_Nixon-Corporations_B3_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON&t=6&akid=3619%2E259176%2ECe4cbt)

**$25.**
If you can believe it, that’s our average contribution online right now. Some give more, but most give a lot less.
We talk a lot about how our movement to end gun violence is fueled by grassroots donors, and we hope this moment of honesty proves that.
When we ask folks to make a donation, we usually ask them to give $3, or $5... maybe even $10. But the truth is, we’re behind on our goals. And today is a day where we need to see a real surge in fundraising to catch up. Election Day is in less than two weeks, and we can’t afford to fall short now.
We have important goals to hit, and they aren’t arbitrary numbers. They’re what we need to raise to send gun safety champions to Congress and other elected offices around the country.

Friends - it's Amy.
My decision to reach out to you today wasn't an easy one - but I don't want to wake up on November 4th wondering if one more message could have tipped the scales.
Because that's how close this race is.
**Experts have said our race for governor is one of the most competitive in the entire country.**
Right now, we're facing a significant budget gap - and it means we're at risk of having to pull the plug on some of our TV ads, just 12 days before the election...
**My finance team pulled the numbers, and if everyone reading this email chipped in $8 or more - we'd be able to keep our ads on air.**
_With Vivek Ramaswamy and his allies pouring in $145 MILLION to their TV ads, and outspending us seven to one, this would be the WORST possible time to have to go dark._
**[That's why I decided to reach out to you today. I know you aren't an ATM, but frankly, I have nowhere else to turn. I'm urgently asking my top supporters to chip in $8 or more to me and Roy Cooper in the next 30 minutes to help us show Vivek Ramaswamy and his billionaire allies the sheer strength of this grassroots campaign.](https://substack.com/redirect/2f2ba12f-b504-4d6f-9264-a90c528e733f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

Amy

In March, when Tim Walz came before a House Oversight hearing on fraud in Minnesota, Jim pressed him hard on the Feeding Our Future scandal. This fight matters to me, too. Fraudsters have stolen from Minnesota programs meant to feed kids and care for our most vulnerable neighbors. Taxpayers here are tired of hearing they have been fleeced. This summer, I authored the National Fraud Enforcement Division Act to make the Justice Department’s new fraud division permanent. It passed the House in September, and every Republican voted for it.Here’s what Jim had to say:

_“Brad Finstad is a farmer, a fighter, and exactly the kind of conservative southern Minnesota needs in Congress. For thirty years after independence, Beirut was "the Paris of the Middle East." The compliment ran in one direction. Hamra Street had its bookshops and cafe terraces where French newspapers sat beside an-Nahar; banks armored by a 1956 secrecy law drank the Gulf's petrodollars; you could ski above the clouds at Faraya and swim off the Corniche the same afternoon. Paris was the measure. Beirut was the echo. No one in 1965 imagined the arrow could swing back around.
This weekend it swung. Around 1,500 businesses wrecked in a night. A 19th-century city hall in Limoges gutted by arson. A tourist office in Lyon torched. Place de la Republique carpeted in dislodged cobbles and glass. Somewhere in the scroll, the caption writes itself -- the one this piece is named for. I pick the phrase up with due suspicion, because Beirut's fall took half a century and France's took a Saturday. But the resemblance being alleged deserves the walk.
resistance
Because the story of how Beirut fell is not a story about a bomb. It is a story about a tempo -- collapse by deferral -- and that tempo is the only thing the analogy imports...

name: Common Sense Tax Team
subject: Missing these tax savings?
body:
Peter, the clock is ticking on 2026. Here are some important tax planning opportunities worth reviewing before year-end.
| |
---
Peter, As we approach the end of 2026, there's one important question worth asking: **Are you taking advantage of every available opportunity to reduce your taxes and keep more of your hard-earned money?** At **Tru-Fit Tax & Planning**, we believe smart tax planning shouldn't start when it's time to file your return. It should happen BEFORE the year ends, while there's still time to make decisions that could potentially save you money. And with several important tax provisions available in 2026, there are some opportunities you won't want to overlook. **HERE ARE 4 AREAS WORTH REVIEWING BEFORE DECEMBER 31:** **1\. Business Owners: Don't Miss Potential Tax Deductions** If you own a business, you may have opportunities to reduce your taxable income through:
* **100% Bonus Depreciation:** Eligible business equipment and other qualifying property may be fully deductible in the year placed in service.
* **Section 179:** Qualifying purchases may be eligible for deductions of up to $2.56 million in 2026, subject to limitations.
* **Qualified Business Income Deduction:** Eligible business owners may deduct up to 20% of qualified business income.

The right strategy could make a meaningful difference in what you owe. **2\. Make the Most of Retirement & Tax-Advantaged Savings** Are you maximizing the accounts that could help reduce your current or future tax burden? For 2026, contribution limits include:
* **401(k):** $24,500, plus additional catch-up contributions if eligible.
* **Traditional & Roth IRAs:** $7,500, plus catch-up contributions for those 50 and older.
* **Health Savings Accounts:** $4,400 for individual coverage or $8,750 for family coverage, if eligible.

Depending on your situation, there may also be opportunities involving Roth conversions or other tax-efficient planning strategies. **3\. Take Another Look at Your State & Local Tax Deductions** If you live in New Jersey or another high-tax state, this one is especially important. For 2026, the federal State and Local Tax (SALT) deduction cap is **$40,400** , with income-based reductions beginning above $505,000 in modified adjusted gross income. Reviewing your property taxes, state income taxes, and other eligible deductions could help identify additional savings opportunities. **4\. Protect Your Wealth & Plan for the Future** Reducing taxes is only part of the equation. It's also important to consider how you're protecting the wealth you've worked hard to build. From strategic gifting and estate planning to reviewing investments and potential capital gains, decisions made today can have an impact for years to come. For 2026, the annual federal gift tax exclusion remains **$19,000 per recipient** , creating opportunities for those considering transferring wealth to family members. **SO, WHAT SHOULD YOU DO BEFORE DECEMBER 31?** Now is a great time to review your financial picture and determine whether opportunities exist to: ✓ Reduce your 2026 tax liability ✓ Maximize eligible business deductions ✓ Review retirement contributions and Roth conversions ✓ Evaluate investment gains and losses ✓ Explore tax-efficient wealth protection strategies ✓ Position yourself for a stronger financial year in 2027 Not every strategy applies to everyone, and some deadlines extend beyond December 31. **That's why having a personalized tax plan matters.** **LET'S FINISH 2026 STRONG!** At Tru-Fit Tax & Planning, our goal is to help you keep more of what you earn, make informed financial decisions, and avoid overlooking valuable tax-saving opportunities. **Don't wait until tax season to discover what you could have done before year-end.** Schedule a complimentary year-end tax planning call with our team to review your situation, explore potential savings, and make a plan for what's ahead. [**BOOK YOUR YEAR-END TAX PLANNING CALL HERE**](https://xtz223.keap-link006.com/v2/click/7e1d1e42adb4983298a3f7af1209be35/eJyNkMFOw0AMRP_F5yxpUiogt6qqqiilBwRntNq4xWLrWBu3aqjy77iA4AISV8-8GY3PoMietW6hgpO-leUUMkgYSAhZFx2rDx9qObsupkUGkfh1lbqDQHX-Ff42XM7F5Ka8zUAHQfM8PswXTb1ZPa_rTWNW8clK_hV0N5n95Czv5_UaxvHPYNyTLo-W3UOl6YCXSS3ZLH1K0fwvqtJXeR58RG7jcBW6fa5b9SeJnpl4l6NQcMa6LakzwbXUh-6IaXBGRSvxIgZ_vajB4bNqfAdczHDH) Let's make sure you're entering 2027 with a strategy, not just a tax return. Best regards, **Rob Gill** Tru-Fit Tax & Planning The Common Sense Tax Team **P.S.** The strategies that save the most have to be in place before year-end. Run your numbers today so you still have time to act on them.

This race will set the stage, and we have two options before us: We can join together, flip Ohio’s must-win seat, and take back the Senate. Or, we can take our foot off the gas in this final sprint, let Husted win, and cede control of the Senate to the GOP until 2029 at least.

I know what I choose, but I can’t win this fight alone.
